AsOfProvenance.description:
Where an `asOf` body came from, and how far the evidence reaches.

Every field but `text` on the parent exists so this answer cannot be
over-read. The corpus holds ONE current text per citation; an earlier one is
RECONSTRUCTED from observed changes, and observation started when it started.

basisChangeId.description: The change event whose before-side supplied this text. Null when `source` is `live`. Pass it to `/us/statutes/section/{actId}/changes` to see the event this answer rests on.
basisChangeId.title: Basischangeid

coverage.description: Prose statement of the same limit, safe to show a reader verbatim.
coverage.title: Coverage

currentVersionEffective.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`. The day the CURRENT text we hold took effect, when the section states one. Present on `observed_change` answers that were checked against it. When it is later than your date, today's text is never served as the law on your date: you get a prior version we hold or `source: unavailable`. Null when the section states no effective date we can read, in which case a `live` answer is UNVERIFIED for your date and the response `note` says so.
currentVersionEffective.title: Currentversioneffective

earliestHeldVersion.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`. The effective date of the earliest version of this section we hold (current or prior). Set on `unavailable` answers that predate the current text, so you can ask for a date we can answer.
earliestHeldVersion.title: Earliestheldversion

editionsObserved.description: `stored_edition` only. Every edition year in which this exact text was observed, enumerated. An ENUMERATION, not a range: a year between the first and last that is absent here is an edition nobody read, and a date resolving to it is reported out of coverage rather than answered from a neighbour.
editionsObserved.title: Editionsobserved

engine.description:
WHICH BACKEND ANSWERED. `asOf` is one parameter over two engines and they make different promises.

`stored_edition`: the answer is a publisher's own printed edition of the text, held verbatim. Used wherever we hold published editions, which today is `corpusType=CFR_ANNUAL` (annual editions per title), the US Code, the Copyright Compendium and OFAC FAQs. The date is resolved to a held edition and that edition's text is returned as printed.

Coverage under this engine is per corpus and is not continuous. The CFR annual editions tile the calendar per title; the others are ENUMERATED editions with gaps between them. A date that falls in a gap returns `source: "unavailable"` with `outOfCoverageReason` and NO text, rather than the neighbouring edition, because the text may have changed in the gap. For the US Code in particular, most dates are currently out of coverage: see `outOfCoverageReason` for which editions we hold.

`observed_change`: the answer is RECONSTRUCTED from changes we observed, and reaches back only as far as capture began for that source. Every other corpus.

Read this before `isBounded`, which does not make the same claim on both engines.
engine.title: Engine

existed.description: False when the earliest thing we ever captured for this section is its ADDITION and that addition postdates your date, so it was not in our corpus yet. A real answer, not a miss. `added` is when our refresh first SAW the section, which for a section older than our capture is later than the law's own start, so read false as 'not held then' rather than proof the law did not exist.
existed.title: Existed

isBounded.description:
⚠️ This flag does not make the same claim on both engines. Read `engine` first.

On `stored_edition`, TRUE means your date falls inside the editions we actually parsed for this title, so the text is a verified published printing rather than an inference. FALSE means out of coverage, and no text is returned.

On `observed_change`, TRUE means: we observed no change affecting your date, and that is not the same as there having been none.

Set when your date predates `observedFrom`, or when we captured no change for this section at all. Change capture began long after the corpus did and is per-source, so a bounded answer is our best reconstruction rather than a verified historical text. Surface it. Rendering a bounded answer as authoritative point-in-time law makes a claim we did not make.
isBounded.title: Isbounded

observedFrom.description: The earliest change we ever captured for this section. Null when we captured none. This is how far back the reconstruction can see, and it is a property of when capture began for this source, not of the age of the law.
observedFrom.title: Observedfrom

outOfCoverageReason.description: Why no text was returned, in a sentence safe to show a reader. Null when text was returned.
outOfCoverageReason.title: Outofcoveragereason

requested.description: The date you asked for, echoed back (`YYYY-MM-DD`). The boundary is END OF DAY, the same as a stored edition and as `changedSince`: a change effective ON this date is already in force that day, so the text returned is the one after it. A change is dated by the publisher's own date when it states one, else by the day we detected it.
requested.title: Requested

resolvedEditionYear.description: `stored_edition` only. The revision year actually served, read from the edition's own printed revision statement. 🔴 This is not always the year the schedule computes: a publisher reprints an unchanged volume into the next year without re-dating it, so the 2024 printing of 4 CFR is the January 1 2019 revision. Render THIS year, never `scheduledEditionYear`.
resolvedEditionYear.title: Resolvededitionyear

scheduledEditionYear.description: `stored_edition` only. The edition the revision schedule says SHOULD cover your date. Differs from `resolvedEditionYear` whenever the publisher reprinted an unchanged volume. Exposed so the disagreement is auditable, not so it can be displayed.
scheduledEditionYear.title: Schedulededitionyear

source.description:
The detail WITHIN the engine above.

On `observed_change` -- `live`: we captured no change to this section after your date, AND the text we hold took effect on or before your date (or states no effective date, in which case the `note` says the answer is unverified). A date that PRECEDES the effective date of the text we hold is never `live`: it is `unavailable` with `outOfCoverageReason`, `currentVersionEffective` and `earliestHeldVersion`, and is refunded. `reconstructed`: rebuilt from the before-side of the first change we captured after your date. `unavailable`: we know it changed but cannot rebuild the earlier text, so no text is returned. That is different from the section being empty, and different again from it not existing.

On `stored_edition` -- `published`: an edition we hold answered, verbatim. `unavailable`: the date is out of coverage for this section and no text is returned, and `outOfCoverageReason` says why in a sentence. Out of coverage means the date falls outside every edition we hold, or inside a gap between two of them; it is never answered from a neighbouring edition.
source.title: Source

AsOfProvenance.title: AsOfProvenance

changeSignal.description:
How this board's source publishes change; read it alongside `lastRetrievedAt`.

`continuous`: the publisher revises the law as it changes, and a refresh that finds a revision emits a change event. Silence on a `current` board means nothing changed.

`edition_only`: the publisher issues periodic editions and we only detect a new edition arriving. Silence means only that no new edition appeared. It is not evidence that the underlying law is unchanged; check the section payload's `currentThrough`.

lastRetrievedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC time of the last refresh run that pulled this source from its publisher and finished cleanly. A run that found nothing new counts. Read it with `cadence`: a date more than one cadence period old means a scheduled run did not confirm the source, so silence on a watch for that board is uninformative. Same value as `/us/statutes/coverage`.

Where this is false the field is never present, on any event, so do not wait for it. Today true only on `cfr`, `federal_rules`. Where true, the date is still unknown for some sections and for every `removed` section; absent always means unknown, so do not substitute `detectedAt`, which can trail the real amendment by months.

ChangeDiffResponse.description:
Old-vs-new text for one change, as whole documents.

``beforeText``/``afterText`` are each the complete text of one version of
the section, not the single chunk that happened to be recorded as that
side's representative. Diff them directly.

``changeKind: "added"`` carries ``afterText`` with no ``beforeText``: there
is nothing to compare a newly published document against, and its full text
is the substance of the notification.

diffAvailable.description: True when this response answers the question its `changeKind` asks: both sides for `amended`, the after side for `added`, the before side for `removed`. False means there is no diff to show (and the call is refunded); `unavailableReason` says why. A side we could not retrieve is never replaced by an invented one.
diffAvailable.title: Diffavailable

unavailableReason.description: Why `diffAvailable` is false. Null when it is true.

relatedActId.description: Set with `lifecycleStage`: the `actId` of the proposed amendment. Fetch it for the proposed text. Omitted for every ordinary change.

sourceChangedOn.description:
The date the publisher records the section as having changed (`YYYY-MM-DD`), e.g. eCFR's per-section `amendment_date`.

Omitted, not null, when we do not have it, and its absence says nothing about the publisher. We carry this date on `cfr`, `federal_rules` and on no other board; `publishesSourceChangedOn` on `GET /boards` tells you which case you are in. Even there it is absent for sections the publisher gives no date for and for every `removed` section.

Absent always means unknown. Do not fall back to `detectedAt`, which can trail the real amendment by months.
sourceChangedOn.title: Sourcechangedon

CitationMissReason.description:
The same finding as one block, for a response that is not itself a citation verdict.

`POST /us/statutes/search` carries it as `citationMissReason`, beside `citationOutsideFilters`:
the query was a citation, the resolver missed, and the ranked results are an ordinary search.

candidates.description: Present only with `missReason: ambiguous_jurisdiction`, and only when we can name the held sections the citation could mean (an acronym two states print, such as `CCR`). At most 10 entries. Pass the right one's `state` to `GET /us/statutes/resolve` to resolve it. Never a pick: when several are listed, none is the answer.

missReason.description: Present only when `resolved` is false and none of `citationOutsideFilters` / `sessionLaw` already explains it. WHY the citation did not resolve: `ambiguous_jurisdiction` (the form is one several jurisdictions print, or names none, and no `state` was given: pass `state`; `candidates` lists the held sections it could mean when we can name them, and never picks one), `out_of_scope_corpus` (it names a body of law this route does not serve; `missReasonHint` says which and where to look), `former_law` (it names a repealed, renumbered or retired compilation we do not serve as current law; `missReasonHint` names the successor where one is known), `malformed` (no parser reads it: a docket or database token, a case or treatise citation, a string with no section number, or a subdivision or edition year with no section before it), `container_not_supported` (it cites a chapter, article, title or part, not a section; this route resolves sections, and answers a container only in the forms `matchLevel: container` lists: browse it with `GET /us/statutes/divisions`, or cite a section inside it), `not_held` (it reads as a citation to a jurisdiction and corpus we serve, and that corpus does not hold the section), `index_warming` (batch items only: the code this citation names was still being read when the call arrived, so there is NO verdict about the citation; the item is not billed, and sending it again in a few seconds answers it), `lookup_failed` (batch items only: the citation resolved, but WE failed to load or serialize its section, so this says nothing about whether the section exists; the item is refunded and counted in the response's `failedCount`, and retrying it answers it). `miss_reason_unavailable` (the check that explains a miss timed out or failed on our side, so this response carries NO explanation: it says nothing about why the citation did not resolve, and resending it usually answers; the citation's own verdict, unresolved, is unchanged and charged as any miss is). A miss is still charged, because the verdict is the product, except `index_warming` and `lookup_failed`, which are not verdicts and are never charged; the reason itself adds no charge. Absent on a resolved citation.

scope.description:
Optional narrowing so this alert covers one citation instead of an entire source. Four mutually exclusive forms. Omit entirely to watch the whole source.

Hierarchy prefix: keys `title`, `chapter`, `part`, `section`, e.g. `{"title": "21", "part": "314"}` for 21 CFR part 314. Every level you set must match. `title` is required whenever any narrower level is set, and `section` also needs `chapter` or `part`. Sources without a title/chapter/part hierarchy return 400 (see `scopable` on `GET /boards`).

Exact section: `{"actId": "CFR_T21_P314_S314_50"}`, using the `actId` from search results and change events. Case-sensitive and validated at create time: an act_id we do not hold, or one from a different source, is a 400. Works on every source, and is the only way to follow a single Federal Register document.

Named source: `{"source": "fdic_fil"}`, for corpora that fold several independent bodies of law behind one `corpusType`. The `agency_guidance` board alone carries 47 named sources across 24 agencies, so an unscoped watch on it delivers FDIC letters, IRS notices, OFAC FAQs and DOE appliance standards together. Accepted on `agency_adjudication`, `agency_guidance`, `agency_manuals`, `cfr`, `federal_rules`; anything else returns 400. Pickable values are on the board's `sources` array in `GET /boards`.

Publishing agency: `{"agency": "irs"}`, covering every source that agency issues on the board (the IRS alone publishes 5 named series). Expanded when an event is matched, not when the watch is created, so a source registered later is covered automatically. Accepted on `agency_adjudication`, `agency_guidance`, `agency_manuals`; pickable values are on the board's `agencies` array in `GET /boards`.

state.description: Board's state (2-letter, case-insensitive). For a federal board (USC, eCFR, the Federal Register) pass `federal` or omit this entirely; the two are equivalent. webhookSecret.description: Optional signing secret, stored encrypted and never returned. When set, every delivery carries an `X-Vaquill-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body bytes, keyed with this secret. To verify, compute the same HMAC over the raw body you received (before parsing JSON) and compare it, constant-time, to the hex digest after `sha256=`. Deliveries also carry Standard Webhooks headers (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature: v1,<base64>`), signed over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`; prefer these, as they add replay protection. The HMAC key is the base64 decoding of the secret after `whsec_` when it has that prefix, otherwise the secret's UTF-8 bytes. `X-Vaquill-Signature` is deprecated but remains in place for at least 12 months.

A state STATUTE chapter, subchapter, title, article or part cited with its container word and a code name we read for that state (`8 Del. C. ch. 1, subch. VII`, `Tex. Penal Code ch. 19`, `N.Y. Penal Law art. 125`, `Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93A`, `La. R.S. Title 14`) also answers `container`, with `section` the first live section in statutory order, but only where we hold that container and its number is unique within the code. A container we do not hold, a missing or unrecognised code name, a regulation or rule set, or a number that repeats in the code (California repeats chapter numbers across its titles) when the citation names more than one level, returns `resolved: false` with `missReason: container_not_supported`. An article that IS the section unit (`La. Civ. Code art. 2315`, `Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 38.23`) is read as a section. To browse chapters, titles and articles use `GET /us/statutes/divisions`. `multiple`: you cited several sections (`§§ 8, 10`, `§§ 1983-1985`) and `section` is the first of them (see `citedSections`), or your citation fits more than one held section (`D.C.COLO.LR 7.1` is both Local Civil and Local Criminal Rule 7.1) and every candidate is listed in `container`; a state statute container number that repeats within its code (`Cal. Penal Code tit. 8` is a title of each of four parts) lists each candidate container's first section there, never picking one, when there are at most 10. `repaired`: the code name you wrote is a recognised miscite and `section` is the one it names (see `repair`); or (`repair.kind: prior_edition`) the text you cited has been replaced by a current one, and `section` is NOT the text you cited: a C.F.R. or U.S.C. section the current code no longer holds, answered with the MOST RECENT historical annual edition we hold, or a superseded rule set whose rule numbers were kept, answered with the current rule (`Tex. R. Civ. Evid. 803` is answered by `Tex. R. Evid. 803`), or a state regulation we hold only as superseded filings, answered with the latest filing (`W. Va. Code R. § 64-14-5`); `repair.interpretedAs` names what was served and why, and `repair.alternatives` lists the other held editions, if any; or (`repair.kind: former_law`, `former_number`) you cited a FORMER section number, recodified or renumbered since, and `section` is the successor the state's own disposition table or history line names, never the former text (a former section split into several answers `multiple`, every successor in `citedSections`). or (`repair.kind: code_name_inferred`) your citation named no code (`CODE ANN. § 73.001`, `Code 4121-3-34`) and `section` is the only one in the state that carries that number, so the code was inferred from the number and not read from your citation; or (`repair.kind: repealed_range`, `renumbered_range`, `range_member`) you cited a New York or California section the publisher printed only inside a run of sections (`6 NYCRR 420.4` inside `420.3 to 420.4`), and `section` is that stub, not the section's own text (`repair.interpretedAs` names the range); `register_reference`: you cited a state register page, and `section` is a rule whose history cites it (see `registerReference`). `resolved` keeps its meaning (a section was returned) and is true at every level; read `matchLevel` to tell an exact section from a first-of-several. Absent for an exact match.

missReason.description: Present only when `resolved` is false and none of `citationOutsideFilters` / `sessionLaw` already explains it. WHY the citation did not resolve: `ambiguous_jurisdiction` (the form is one several jurisdictions print, or names none, and no `state` was given: pass `state`; `candidates` lists the held sections it could mean when we can name them, and never picks one), `out_of_scope_corpus` (it names a body of law this route does not serve; `missReasonHint` says which and where to look), `former_law` (it names a repealed, renumbered or retired compilation we do not serve as current law; `missReasonHint` names the successor where one is known), `malformed` (no parser reads it: a docket or database token, a case or treatise citation, a string with no section number, or a subdivision or edition year with no section before it), `container_not_supported` (it cites a chapter, article, title or part, not a section; this route resolves sections, and answers a container only in the forms `matchLevel: container` lists: browse it with `GET /us/statutes/divisions`, or cite a section inside it), `not_held` (it reads as a citation to a jurisdiction and corpus we serve, and that corpus does not hold the section), `index_warming` (batch items only: the code this citation names was still being read when the call arrived, so there is NO verdict about the citation; the item is not billed, and sending it again in a few seconds answers it), `lookup_failed` (batch items only: the citation resolved, but WE failed to load or serialize its section, so this says nothing about whether the section exists; the item is refunded and counted in the response's `failedCount`, and retrying it answers it). `miss_reason_unavailable` (the check that explains a miss timed out or failed on our side, so this response carries NO explanation: it says nothing about why the citation did not resolve, and resending it usually answers; the citation's own verdict, unresolved, is unchanged and charged as any miss is). A miss is still charged, because the verdict is the product, except `index_warming` and `lookup_failed`, which are not verdicts and are never charged; the reason itself adds no charge. Absent on a resolved citation.

pinpointMatch.description: Present only when the row's `pinpoint` is non-empty, it resolved, and `resolve` was on. The unit that pinpoint names, located inside the resolved section. The subsection a pinpoint names, located inside the returned section. ALWAYS read `matched` (or `matchLevel`) before using `text` or `fullText`: when the section has no such subsection the block says so rather than staying silent, and under `matchLevel: ancestor` the text fields describe the deepest unit that DOES exist (read `unmatched` for the part of your pinpoint that did not). `path` is the machine form of the pinpoint, one entry per level. `(f)(1.5)` is `["f", "1.5"]` and `(d-1)` is `["d-1"]`, so a label that contains a dot or a hyphen is never split. `text` is the unit's own text (its lead-in when it has children), `fullText` is the unit with everything beneath it exactly as printed, and `leadIn` is each ancestor's own text in order, so a deeply nested unit can be read as the sentence it completes. `charStart` / `charEnd` index into the `plain` text of `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}/body` (see `structure.textSha256`). No extra charge.

matchedTerms.description: Which of your query's words the unit carries, in the order you wrote them. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
matchedTerms.title: Matchedterms

note.description: A sentence saying why no subsection is named, when `located` is false. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
note.title: Note

path.description: The named unit's path, one entry per level: `(f)(1.5)` is `["f", "1.5"]` and `(d-1)` is `["d-1"]`, so a label that contains a dot or a hyphen is never split. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
path.title: Path

pinpoint.description: The unit as a pinpoint, outermost label first. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
pinpoint.title: Pinpoint

reason.description: Present when `located` is false. `no_single_unit`: your query's words do not point at one subsection. `no_structure`: we could not recover this section's outline. `text_unavailable` and `section_too_long`: the text could not be read or is too long to outline here. `lookup_failed`: it failed this time; the section is unaffected. `not_looked_up`: this request ran out of time for pinpoints. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
reason.title: Reason

scope.description: `unit`: this unit matched. `parent`: several of its sub-units matched equally well, so the block names their common parent rather than choosing between them. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
scope.title: Scope

structure.description: Where the section's outline came from and how far it can be trusted. Omitted from the response when it has no value.

text.description: The unit's own text, without its sub-units. It can read as a fragment: add `leadIn` to read the sentence it completes. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
text.title: Text

SearchHitPinpoint.title: SearchHitPinpoint

SectionEnactment.description: One printed entry of a publisher's table: this act, against this section.

actSectionAsPrinted.description: Which section of the ACT does it, as printed (Washington's `1223`, Kentucky's `5`). Null where the table prints none.
actSectionAsPrinted.title: Actsectionasprinted

action.description: What the act did to the section, normalised: `added`, `amended`, `repealed`, `renumbered`, or `other`. It is mapped from `actionAsPrinted` only where the publisher's legend is settled; `other` means the table prints no action (Nebraska, `actionAsPrinted` is null), prints one that is not a change to this section (Mississippi's `BF`, brought forward), or one we do not map. Never read `other` as 'unchanged'. The publisher's own code is always in `actionAsPrinted`.
action.title: Action

actionAsPrinted.description: The publisher's own action code or word for this entry, verbatim. Null when the table prints none.
actionAsPrinted.title: Actionasprinted

approvedDate.description: Date the governor approved the act, ISO 8601: never an effective date. Null when none is held.
approvedDate.title: Approveddate

basis.description: Where the entry comes from. `publisher_sections_affected`: the publisher's own table of the code sections an act affects. `credit_line`: the section's own history credit cites the act, and the citation names exactly one act we hold; weaker evidence, and it states no action. Never read out of the act's prose.
basis.title: Basis

citation.description: The act's citation as its publisher prints it. Null when none is held.
citation.title: Citation

citeAsPrinted.description: Set only on `basis: credit_line` rows: the session-law citation exactly as the section's credit line prints it. Null on `publisher_sections_affected` rows.
citeAsPrinted.title: Citeasprinted

codeAsPrinted.description: The code the publisher qualifies the section with, as printed (`HRS`, `D.C. Code`, `Education Code`). Null where the publisher prints none.
codeAsPrinted.title: Codeasprinted

effectiveDates.description: Every effective date the publisher prints for the ACT, in printed order: the act's, not necessarily this section's (an act can take effect in parts, and a date may carry a `scopeAsPrinted`). Empty when none is held, which does not mean the act is not in force.
effectiveDates.title: Effectivedates

enactmentOutcome.description: How the act became (or did not become) law, as on the act's record: `signed`, `vetoed` and so on. Null when it is not recorded.
enactmentOutcome.title: Enactmentoutcome

href.description: Path of the act on this API: `GET` it for the record, or its `/body` for the text.
href.title: Href

identityConfidence.description: How firmly the registry knows the act is the law it says it is: `confirmed`, `single_source`, `inferred` or `disputed`.
identityConfidence.title: Identityconfidence

matchQuality.description: How the entry was matched. `as_printed` (publisher table rows): the printed section equals this section's number after folding case, spacing, dashes and the section sign, and nothing is matched by prefix. `credit_cite_unique` (credit-line rows): the credit's citation resolved to exactly one act in the same state with a numbering year within one year of the cited one; a citation that fits several acts is dropped, never guessed. Neither is a legal analysis of what the act did.
matchQuality.title: Matchquality

printedEntryCount.description: How many printed entries of the publisher's table were folded into this one entry. An act appears once however many times its table lists the section (a second spelling of the number, or two sections of the act amending it); above 1 means `actionAsPrinted` and `actSectionAsPrinted` may list several values.
printedEntryCount.title: Printedentrycount

sectionAsPrinted.description: The section exactly as the publisher's table prints it.
sectionAsPrinted.title: Sectionasprinted

sectionsTouchedCount.description: Set only when `title` was shortened: how many code sections the act's own title lists. An omnibus act is titled by every section it amends; `title` then keeps the section asked about and counts the rest. Null when the title is served as printed.
sectionsTouchedCount.title: Sectionstouchedcount

sessionCode.description: The session the act was enacted in, as in `coverage.sessionsHeld`.
sessionCode.title: Sessioncode

sessionLawId.description: The act, in the session-law registry. Read it at `href`.
sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid

textStatus.description: Whether we serve the act's text: `held`, `withheld`, `not_held` or `pending`, as on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.
textStatus.title: Textstatus

title.description: The act's title as printed. Null when none is held.
examples: AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE A PERSON WHO IS THE HOLDER OF A WINE MANUFACTURER'S PERMIT
title.title: Title

titleCompacted.description: True when `title` is a shortened display form. The full title is on the act: `GET` `href`.
titleCompacted.title: Titlecompacted

SectionEnactment.title: SectionEnactment

actId.description: The section's act_id as served, after any citation or copy damage was resolved.
actId.title: Actid

coverage.description: What this answer is read from, and what it is not. Show it with the list.

creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price. 0 when `supported` is false (refunded) and on a failure. A citation sent in place of the act_id adds the `/us/statutes/resolve` price when it resolves; a citation that resolves to nothing is refunded in full, the `/us/statutes/resolve` price included.
creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed

enactments.description: The acts the publisher's tables list against this section, newest act first (by approval date, undated last), ONE ENTRY PER ACT AND ACTION (`printedEntryCount` says how many printed entries were folded into it). This is the whole chain of acts we can link to the section, while the section record's own `history` is only its latest amendment. NEVER a complete history: only acts we hold, in sessions we hold, whose table lists the section in the printed form this jurisdiction's mapping reads. Empty with `supported: true` is a real answer: no held table lists it.
enactments.title: Enactments

jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the section's jurisdiction. Null for a federal section.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.
processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems

reason.description: Why `supported` is false. `unsupported_jurisdiction`: we do not read this jurisdiction's table (none is printed, or its form is not verified against our section numbers), see `coverage.note`. `not_a_state_code_section`: the section is not a state statute (a federal, regulation or constitution section). `section_not_in_proven_form`: the jurisdiction is read, but this section's stored number is not in a form the mapping was proven on, so it is not guessed at. `section_number_missing`: the stored section carries no number to look up. `section_citation_mismatch`: the stored section number and the stored citation disagree (or the citation is not in the printed shape), so neither is trusted. `code_unknown` / `code_not_proven`: the section sits in a code (California, Hawaii, DC) we cannot name, or one whose printed form was not proven against our section numbers. Null when `supported` is true.
reason.title: Reason

resolvedFrom.description: Present only when your input was a citation or an id carrying copy damage: what it was matched as. Null when you sent an exact act_id.

supported.description: True when this section's jurisdiction is one whose publisher table is mapped to the statutes section numbers and this section is in the form that mapping was proven on, or one whose credit lines are read for session-law citations: then `enactments` is an answer, even when it is empty, and the call is charged. False when it is not (see `reason`): `enactments` is empty, says nothing about the section, and the call is NOT charged.
supported.title: Supported

truncated.description: True when more entries matched than are returned (the newest are kept). A section amended by that many acts is not a case we have met.
truncated.title: Truncated

SectionIdentifierResolution.description:
How the identifier you sent was matched, when it was not an exact act_id.

Present only when the input did NOT match as sent. Absent (null) means the
section is exactly the act_id in your request.

actId.description: The act_id it matched. Send this next time to skip resolution.
actId.title: Actid

citedSections.description: Set with `matchLevel: multiple`. The sections your citation named, as written (a range such as `1983-1985` is one entry); `section` is the first. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
citedSections.title: Citedsections

container.description: Set with `matchLevel: container`. What you cited and the sections inside it; `section` is the first of them. Also set with `matchLevel: multiple` when the citation fits several held sections and none is the one cited (kind `alternatives`): every candidate is listed, `section` is only the first offered. Omitted from the response when it has no value.

input.description: The identifier exactly as you sent it.
input.title: Input

matchLevel.description: Present only when `section` is NOT the exact unit you cited. `container`: you cited a container in one of the supported forms (a Missouri, New Jersey, West Virginia or Wyoming regulation series or chapter, a constitution article or amendment, an Indiana chapter, an Illinois article, or a U.S. Code chapter such as `18 U.S.C. ch. 96`; a U.S. Code subchapter is not read), and `section` is the FIRST section inside it (see `container` for how many there are and what they are). A state STATUTE chapter, subchapter, title, article or part cited with its container word and a code name we read for that state (`8 Del. C. ch. 1, subch. VII`, `Tex. Penal Code ch. 19`, `N.Y. Penal Law art. 125`, `Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93A`, `La. R.S. Title 14`) also answers `container`, with `section` the first live section in statutory order, but only where we hold that container and its number is unique within the code. A container we do not hold, a missing or unrecognised code name, a regulation or rule set, or a number that repeats in the code (California repeats chapter numbers across its titles) when the citation names more than one level, returns `resolved: false` with `missReason: container_not_supported`. An article that IS the section unit (`La. Civ. Code art. 2315`, `Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 38.23`) is read as a section. To browse chapters, titles and articles use `GET /us/statutes/divisions`. `multiple`: you cited several sections (`§§ 8, 10`, `§§ 1983-1985`) and `section` is the first of them (see `citedSections`), or your citation fits more than one held section (`D.C.COLO.LR 7.1` is both Local Civil and Local Criminal Rule 7.1) and every candidate is listed in `container`; a state statute container number that repeats within its code (`Cal. Penal Code tit. 8` is a title of each of four parts) lists each candidate container's first section there, never picking one, when there are at most 10. `repaired`: the code name you wrote is a recognised miscite and `section` is the one it names (see `repair`); or (`repair.kind: prior_edition`) the text you cited has been replaced by a current one, and `section` is NOT the text you cited: a C.F.R. or U.S.C. section the current code no longer holds, answered with the MOST RECENT historical annual edition we hold, or a superseded rule set whose rule numbers were kept, answered with the current rule (`Tex. R. Civ. Evid. 803` is answered by `Tex. R. Evid. 803`), or a state regulation we hold only as superseded filings, answered with the latest filing (`W. Va. Code R. § 64-14-5`); `repair.interpretedAs` names what was served and why, and `repair.alternatives` lists the other held editions, if any; or (`repair.kind: former_law`, `former_number`) you cited a FORMER section number, recodified or renumbered since, and `section` is the successor the state's own disposition table or history line names, never the former text (a former section split into several answers `multiple`, every successor in `citedSections`). or (`repair.kind: code_name_inferred`) your citation named no code (`CODE ANN. § 73.001`, `Code 4121-3-34`) and `section` is the only one in the state that carries that number, so the code was inferred from the number and not read from your citation; or (`repair.kind: repealed_range`, `renumbered_range`, `range_member`) you cited a New York or California section the publisher printed only inside a run of sections (`6 NYCRR 420.4` inside `420.3 to 420.4`), and `section` is that stub, not the section's own text (`repair.interpretedAs` names the range); `register_reference`: you cited a state register page, and `section` is a rule whose history cites it (see `registerReference`). `resolved` keeps its meaning (a section was returned) and is true at every level; read `matchLevel` to tell an exact section from a first-of-several. Absent for an exact match.
matchLevel.title: Matchlevel

registerReference.description: Present only when `matchLevel` is `register_reference`: the citation names a page, issue or filing of a state register or bulletin. When `registerItemHeld` is true `section` IS that register item (corpusType STATE_REGISTER, a notice as printed, not codified law). Otherwise the item is not held and `section` is a RULE whose history note cites it (the first of `ruleCount`, in document order); read `rules` for the others.

repair.description: Set with `matchLevel: repaired`. The miscite we corrected and how we read it. Omitted from the response when it has no value.

subsection.description: The pincite your citation carried, e.g. `(h)(11)` for `26 U.S.C. § 1(h)(11)`. The whole section is served; use `pinpoint=(h)(11)` on `/body` to get that subsection, or `structured=true` for the whole tree.
subsection.title: Subsection

via.description: `citation` -- your input was a citation, resolved with the same resolver as `GET /us/statutes/resolve`. Check it the way you would check a `/resolve` answer. `normalized_id` -- your input was an act_id carrying surrounding whitespace, quotes, a trailing period or double percent-encoding, which were removed.
via.title: Via

SectionIdentifierResolution.title: SectionIdentifierResolution

resolvedFrom.description: Present when the identifier sent was not the act_id served.

SessionLawBatchLaw.description: One served law: the same record `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` returns.

amendatoryMarkup.description: Whether the language an amending act strikes and inserts survives in the text. `preserved`: it is in `text`, in the convention `markupConvention` names. `lost`: the publisher printed it and our text does not keep it, so deleted words can read as law: check the source before quoting. `absent`: the act carries no such markup that we found. `not_applicable`: there is no text to carry it.
amendatoryMarkup.title: Amendatorymarkup

approvedDate.description: Date the governor (or the equivalent authority) approved the act, ISO 8601. Never an effective date: an act is usually in force on a different day, which is `effectiveDates`. Null when the publisher prints no approval date. Where the registry holds none but the publisher's own dated label on `otherDates` names the governor's signature, it is filled from that label and `approvedDateDerived` is true. The `approvedFrom` and `approvedTo` filters do NOT match a derived date: they read the registry's own approval date.
approvedDate.title: Approveddate

approvedDateDerived.description: True only when `approvedDate` was not held as an approval date and we filled it from a dated label printed on the act (today South Dakota's `Signed by the Governor`, listed under `otherDates`), on an act whose `enactmentOutcome` is `signed` or `line_item_veto`. False when `approvedDate` is null or is the registry's own. We never read a `presented` or `passed` date as an approval, nor a signing label on an act that became law without signature.
approvedDateDerived.title: Approveddatederived

billKey.description: Normalised bill identifier (chamber and type letters plus the number) that stands in for a chapter number in states that do not number their acts (Missouri, Ohio, Nebraska). `House Bill 2` is `HB2`. Null whenever `number` is set. Part of the `sessionLawId` as `B<billKey>`.
billKey.title: Billkey

billNumber.description: The bill the act originated as, as the publisher prints it. Matches as a citation on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.
billNumber.title: Billnumber

body.description: The first page of the law's text exactly as printed, present only when `includeBody` was true and the text is served. Null otherwise, and then not charged; `bodyNote` says why. Read `bodyHasMore` to know whether the act continues.
examples:
CHAPTER 1--S.F.No. 1552

An act

relating to agriculture; ...
body.title: Body

bodyHasMore.description: True when the text continues beyond `body`. Each further page is read, and charged, on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`. Null when `body` is null.
bodyHasMore.title: Bodyhasmore

bodyNextCursor.description: Send as `cursor` to `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body` to read the next page of this law. Null on the last page, and when `body` is null.
bodyNextCursor.title: Bodynextcursor

bodyNote.description: Why `body` is null although `includeBody` was true, as a token: `withheld` or `pending` (the text is not served), `not_held` (we hold no text), `empty_text`, `read_failed` (the read of this law's text failed: not charged, repeat the call or read `/body`), `unaffordable` or `charge_failed` (the bodies could not be paid for, see the response's `bodyNote`). Omitted when `body` is present or `includeBody` was not sent.
bodyNote.title: Bodynote

bodyPageEnd.description: Character offset just past `body` in the full text: the first page starts at 0. Null when `body` is null.
bodyPageEnd.title: Bodypageend

bodyTotalChars.description: Length of the whole text in characters. Null when `body` is null.
bodyTotalChars.title: Bodytotalchars

charCount.description: Length of the law's full text in characters, the same as `totalChars` on the body. Null when there is no text. It is reported for a withheld law too (a fact about the text we hold), though that text is not served.
charCount.title: Charcount

citableAs.description: The law cited the way a lawyer writes it, from the state's own form: `Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `2025 Fla. Laws ch. 3`, `Ill. Pub. Act 104-0001`, `S.L. 2025-12` (North Carolina), `Stats. 2025, ch. 12` (California), `Ohio S.B. 1 (2025)` for a state that numbers no chapters. A law in a special or extraordinary session carries it (`Minn. Laws 2025, 1st Spec. Sess., ch. 1`). Every value is read back through the grammar that `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` accepts a citation in, and must name this law; one that would not is null, never guessed. Null where the state's form is not known, for a series with no standard form (resolutions, memorials), or for a law with neither a chapter nor a bill key. Where a regular and a special session each have a chapter 1, the bare form is the regular session's law and resolves with that law flagged as the default; the special session's carries its session. Distinct from `citation`, which is the publisher's printed form.
citableAs.title: Citableas

citation.description: The act's citation as its publisher prints it, falling back to `{session label}, ch. {number}` when none is printed. It is NOT unique: many states print a bare `CHAPTER 1` every session. Key on `sessionLawId`.
citation.title: Citation

citationAsPrinted.description: The citation exactly as the publisher prints it. Null when none is printed.
citationAsPrinted.title: Citationasprinted

citationShort.description: A compact label for tables and badges: `MN ch. 1 (2025)`, `IL P.A. 104-0001`, `OH S.B. 1 (2025)`. Not a form to send back: use `citableAs` or the `sessionLawId`. Null exactly when `citableAs` is null.
citationShort.title: Citationshort

codeSectionsAffected.description: The code sections the publisher's own table lists the act as affecting, as printed. Always a list. Empty when the publisher prints no such table, which is common: the title still names sections in prose. We do not read sections out of the act text into this list.
codeSectionsAffected.title: Codesectionsaffected

documentKind.description: What kind of document the text was taken from: `session_law_print` (the publisher's printed chapter), `enrolled_bill`, `slip_law`, `volume_extract` (carved out of a bound volume) or `other`. An open list. Null when there is no text.
documentKind.title: Documentkind

effectiveDates.description: Every effective date the publisher prints for the act, in printed order. Always a list, never null; empty when none is held. Empty does NOT mean the act is not in force: a date printed as a rule (`the day following final enactment`) or not printed in the publisher's metadata is not guessed, and the approval date is never substituted for it. An act can take effect in parts, so a date may carry a `scopeAsPrinted`.
effectiveDates.title: Effectivedates

effectiveFirst.description: Earliest of the act's effective dates we hold. Null when we hold none: a date the publisher does not print, or prints as a relative rule (`the day following final enactment`), is not guessed. The full list is `effectiveDates` on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.
effectiveFirst.title: Effectivefirst

effectiveLast.description: Latest of the act's effective dates we hold. Equal to `effectiveFirst` for an act with one date; null when we hold none.
effectiveLast.title: Effectivelast

enactmentOutcome.description: How the measure became, or failed to become, law. `signed`; `became_law_without_signature`; `veto_overridden`; `line_item_veto` (signed with some items vetoed); `vetoed` and `pocket_veto` (not law); `not_presented` (no governor action recorded, usual for resolutions); `approved_by_voters`; `unknown` (the publisher does not say).
enactmentOutcome.title: Enactmentoutcome

estimatedBodyPages.description: The most body pages the text can take, so the price of reading the whole law is at most this times the body price. A page holds up to 30,000 characters but is cut back to a paragraph break, so it can be as short as 24,001; the estimate counts every page but the last at that shortest size, so a long act usually takes fewer pages than this and never more. Text that fits one page is 1. Present when the text can be read: `textStatus` is `held`, or `withheld` for a reason we can label (read it with `includeUnverified=true` on `/body`). Null otherwise. Reading a whole law costs `estimatedBodyPages` times the price of one body page (6 credits per page on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`); most acts are a page or two.
estimatedBodyPages.title: Estimatedbodypages

extrasUnavailable.description: Present and `true` only when the read behind `publisher`, `provenance` and `session.coverageStatus` failed on this request. Those three are then absent because we could not read them, not because the act has none: repeat the request to get them. Omitted when the read succeeded.
extrasUnavailable.title: Extrasunavailable

identityConfidence.description: How firmly the law's identity (session and number) is established. `single_source`: read from one publisher source, which is every state law at launch. `confirmed`: agreed by a second independent source, the level at which a `lawId` can be minted. `inferred`: derived by us rather than printed. `disputed`: sources disagree. The `sessionLawId` is the same at every level.
identityConfidence.title: Identityconfidence

input.description: The entry of your `ids` this law answers, exactly as you sent it (trimmed). When two entries name the same law, the law appears once, under the first.
input.title: Input

instrumentType.description: What kind of measure this is: `act`, `joint_resolution`, `concurrent_resolution`, `resolution`, `resolve`, `memorial` or `other`. An open list. A resolution that was numbered and published among the session laws is included, with `isLaw` saying whether it binds as law.
instrumentType.title: Instrumenttype

isLaw.description: True for an act that is law. False for a numbered measure that is not: a vetoed bill, a pocket veto. Null when `enactmentOutcome` does not settle it (`not_presented`, `unknown`).
isLaw.title: Islaw

jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`. Federal acts are not served by this family: they are on `/us/statutes/section`.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

lawId.description: The law's identifier in the open us1 scheme. Null until its identity is confirmed by a second source and the us1 state shape is minted, so it is null on every state law today. Use `sessionLawId`, which is always present.
lawId.title: Lawid

licenseNote.description: What the law's licence class is and what it means for reuse, in a plain sentence: `Government public: published by a government body with no restrictive terms, so the text may be reused, including commercially.` Every law served with text is of a class that permits reuse; a note saying otherwise describes a record whose text is held back. Free text to show, not an enum to branch on: branch on `textStatus`.
examples: Government public: published by a government body with no restrictive terms, so the text may be reused, including commercially.
licenseNote.title: Licensenote

markupConvention.description: How preserved markup is written, set only when `amendatoryMarkup` is `preserved`. `wdiff`: deleted language is `[-like this-]` and inserted language `{+like this+}`. `publisher_literal`: the publisher's own words are left as printed (Minnesota prints `new text begin` / `new text end` and `deleted text begin` / `deleted text end` markers). `mixed`: both in one text.
markupConvention.title: Markupconvention

number.description: The chapter or act number exactly as printed, as a string. It is not always an integer: `1`, `2025-12` (Florida), `104-0001` (Illinois), `1A`. Null where the state does not number its acts (see `billKey`).
number.title: Number

numberingYear.description: The year of the numbering sequence the chapter number belongs to, where the state numbers by year (Minnesota, Florida, Texas). It appears in the `sessionLawId` as `_Y2025`. A chapter number is only unique within a session and numbering year: Minnesota's regular and first special sessions of 2025 each have a Chapter 1. Null where one sequence runs across the session (Louisiana).
numberingYear.title: Numberingyear

officialUrl.description: The PUBLISHER's page for this act, never a Vaquill URL: where a person goes to read the act at its legislature. Where the legislature keeps one page per bill (California, Virginia, New York) it is that page, rebuilt from the session and bill number, so it is present for a law we hold back or only know of. Elsewhere it is the government file the text was collected from (`sourceUrl`), which can be a volume covering many acts. `officialUrlBasis` says which. Null when we hold neither. Our own copy of the text is `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`, a Vaquill service, and is never reported here.
officialUrl.title: Officialurl

officialUrlBasis.description: How `officialUrl` was found: `bill_page` (the publisher's page for this one act) or `text_source` (the government file the text came from, possibly shared by many acts). Null with `officialUrl`.
officialUrlBasis.title: Officialurlbasis

otherDates.description: Every other date printed on the act, each with its `kind`: the approval date, filing dates and the publisher's own milestones (presentment to the governor).
otherDates.title: Otherdates

pageCount.description: Pages in the source document when it is a PDF. Null for HTML sources.
pageCount.title: Pagecount

provenance.description: How we came by the text (the extraction method, the bound volume it was cut from) and the collector's own `caveats` on the record. Omitted, not null, when it cannot be read or we only know the act exists.

publisher.description: What the publisher itself printed or published about the act, beyond the dates and citation above: its own structured fields verbatim (`publisherFields`: the bill's action history, committees, sponsors, and vote counts where the publisher gives them), its own identifiers, the legislature number and the printed pages. Omitted, not null, when it cannot be read or we only know the act exists.

series.description: The numbering series the law belongs to within its session. Most states have one, `general`. Others number acts, resolutions or local laws separately (`public`, `act`, `acts`, `law`, `public_act`, `resolve`, `resolution_chapter`, `local`, ...). An open list that grows as jurisdictions load. Filter with `series` on the list.

sessionLawId.description: Permanent identifier of the law, the key to use everywhere. Shape `SSL_{state}_{session code}_{series}[_Y{numberingYear}]_{C<chapter>|B<billKey>}`. It never changes: a correction to our reading of a law keeps the old id working. Pass it to `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

shortTitle.description: The act's short title when the publisher gives one (Ohio, New York, the District of Columbia and a few others do), otherwise null.

sourceUrl.description: The official page or file the act's text was collected from, on a government publisher's host: the first `sources` entry whose `role` is `text` and whose `hostClass` is `gov`. Open it to verify the text against the publisher. Null when we hold no such source (a law we know exists and have not collected) or when the text source is not a government host. Present on a withheld law too: the official copy is always where to go when we hold the text back.

sources.description: The publisher documents the record was collected from, with the hash and fetch time of each: the audit trail from this response back to the official copy.

title.description: The act's long title as printed, usually beginning `An act relating to`. It names the code sections the act amends in prose.
examples: An act relating to agriculture; modifying financial reporting requirements for grain buyers; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 223.17, subdivision 6.

withheldReason.description: Present only when `textStatus` is `withheld`: a plain sentence saying what is wrong with the text we hold and what would release it. Free text, not an enum: show it, do not branch on it. The record itself (dates, sources, title) is still served and still correct.

didYouMean.description: Real `sessionLawId`s the entry points at: the one that exists in another case, or every law an ambiguous citation names (at most 20, the conventional reading first). Empty when nothing matched.

reason.description: The finer reason, the same vocabulary as `reason` on the 404 of `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`: `not_in_registry`, `wrong_case`, `unresolved_citation`, `ambiguous_citation`, `needs_jurisdiction`, `federal_session_law`, `missing_session_law_id`, `session_not_fully_collected`; or `lookup_failed` when `status` is `error`. Branch on `status`, which is the closed set; the wording of a reason can grow.

sessionCoverage.description: On `session_not_fully_collected`, the partly collected session the entry points into: how many laws we hold of how many it should have. Null otherwise.

status.description: `not_found`: no law carries this id (or it exists in another letter case, see `didYouMean`). `unparsed`: it reads as a citation and no state session law we hold carries it. `ambiguous`: the citation names several laws of one state, all in `didYouMean`, none chosen for you. `needs_jurisdiction`: the citation is in a form several states share and names none; `jurisdictions` lists where it exists. `session_not_fully_collected`: nothing matched and the session it points into is only partly collected, so the law may exist; `sessionCoverage` says how much we hold. `federal`: a federal act, served by `/us/statutes/section`. `error`: we failed to look this entry up; it is NOT a statement that the law does not exist, it is refunded in full, and it is safe to send again.

truncated.description: True when `didYouMean` was capped and `candidateCount` is larger. Null otherwise.

ids.description: State session law ids, or citations, to read: up to 50 DISTINCT entries per call. Each entry is read exactly as the `{sessionLawId}` path of `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` reads one: an id as sent, an id carrying copy damage, or a citation (`Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `P.A. 104-0001`, `S.F.No. 1552`). Entries are trimmed, and blank ones are dropped. Duplicates collapse FIRST (the first spelling wins, order is kept) and the cap applies to what is left, so a list quoting one law sixty times is one entry; `deduped` says how many were collapsed. 200 is the ceiling on the raw list. An entry is at most 300 characters. Federal ids (`SAL_...`) and endpoint names are misses, never charged. A CITATION also pays the resolve price (2 credits) whether it resolves or not, because the lookup is the verdict: an unresolved, ambiguous or state-less citation keeps it. It is refunded only when the session is partly collected or we failed. An id never pays it.
ids.title: Ids

includeBody.description: Return the FIRST page of each served law's text inline, on `body`, beside the record. A page is about 30,000 characters and costs the ordinary body price (6 credits) per law whose page is served; a law whose text is withheld, not held or empty comes back with `body: null` and is not charged for it. Read `creditsConsumed` rather than computing the total: the worst case is 50 laws at 2 + 6 credits each. `bodyNextCursor` continues a longer act on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`.
includeBody.title: Includebody

jurisdiction.description: Optional two-letter state code that scopes how a CITATION in `ids` is read, for the whole batch: it supplies the state a citation does not name (`Laws 2025, ch. 1` with `mn` is Minnesota's) and vetoes a state the citation does name or whose form belongs to another. Ignored for an id. Takes the 56 jurisdictions (the 50 states, `dc` and the territories `pr`, `gu`, `vi`, `as`, `mp`), case-insensitive; `federal` or an unknown code is a 422 and nothing is charged. Omit it for a batch whose citations each name their own state.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

bodyNote.description: Set only when `includeBody` was sent and the bodies were withheld for the whole call: either your balance could not cover them, or the charge for them could not be completed on our side. Either way no body was returned and none was charged, and the laws are intact. Absent otherwise.
bodyNote.title: Bodynote

creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price: 2 per law served, plus the 2-credit resolve price for each citation whose resolution is kept, plus the body price per `body` served. Misses and failures bill nothing for the route.
creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed

deduped.description: How many entries of `ids` were collapsed because an earlier entry was identical after trimming. Zero when none were. Two DIFFERENT spellings of one law are not counted here: the law appears once in `laws` and both spellings are in `resolved`.
deduped.title: Deduped

laws.description: The served laws, one per distinct law, in the order the entries of `ids` first reached them. Entries that missed are NOT here, so a client mapping by position must use `input` on each law (or `notFound`), never the index.
laws.title: Laws

notFound.description: Every entry that did not yield a law, in the order sent, each with its `status` and `reason`. A miss is not charged for the route's own price. An entry read as a CITATION also paid the resolve price, kept whenever we gave a verdict on it (`unparsed`, `ambiguous`, `needs_jurisdiction`, `federal`) and refunded on `session_not_fully_collected` and `error`. An id pays no resolve price.
notFound.title: Notfound

processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.
processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems

resolved.description: One entry per input that did NOT match an id exactly as sent: a citation resolved to its law, or an id cleaned of whitespace, quotes or a trailing period. Includes an input whose law an earlier entry already produced, so every input is mappable onto `laws`. Empty when every entry was an exact id.
resolved.title: Resolved

amendatoryMarkup.description: Whether the language an amending act strikes and inserts survives in the text. `preserved`: it is in `text`, in the convention `markupConvention` names. `lost`: the publisher printed it and our text does not keep it, so deleted words can read as law: check the source before quoting. `absent`: the act carries no such markup that we found. `not_applicable`: there is no text to carry it.
amendatoryMarkup.title: Amendatorymarkup

approvedDate.description: Date the governor approved the act, ISO 8601, as on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`: never an effective date. Null when none is held. See `approvedDateDerived`.
approvedDate.title: Approveddate

approvedDateDerived.description: True only when `approvedDate` was filled from the publisher's dated signature label rather than held as the approval date. See the same field on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.
approvedDateDerived.title: Approveddatederived

available.description: False when we do not serve this law's text; `reason` says why. A page with `available: false` is not charged.
available.title: Available

citation.description: The act's citation as its publisher prints it, the same as `citation` on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`. Carried here so a page is attributable on its own, with no second call.
citation.title: Citation

creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price. It includes the `/us/statutes/resolve` fee when a citation was sent where an id goes. 0 when the call was not charged or was refunded (a body that answers `available: false`).
creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed

estimatedRemainingCredits.description: The most credits to read the rest of the text from `pageEnd`: the most pages still to come (counted at the shortest size a page can be cut back to) times the price of a page. 0 on the last page. Null when no text is served. An upper bound that is never below what reading the rest costs. Reading a whole law costs `estimatedBodyPages` times the price of one body page (6 credits per page on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`); most acts are a page or two.
estimatedRemainingCredits.title: Estimatedremainingcredits

hasMore.description: True when more pages follow; fetch them with `nextCursor`. Each page is charged.
hasMore.title: Hasmore

isCurrentVersion.description: True when `version` is the version `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` serves now. Present with `version`.
isCurrentVersion.title: Iscurrentversion

jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

markupConvention.description: How preserved markup is written, set only when `amendatoryMarkup` is `preserved`. `wdiff`: deleted language is `[-like this-]` and inserted language `{+like this+}`. `publisher_literal`: the publisher's own words are left as printed (Minnesota prints `new text begin` / `new text end` and `deleted text begin` / `deleted text end` markers). `mixed`: both in one text.
markupConvention.title: Markupconvention

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page: send it as `cursor` on the same path. Null on the last page. It is tied to this exact text, so a cursor from before the text was re-collected is a 409.
nextCursor.title: Nextcursor

notice.description: One plain sentence saying what is uncertain about this text and what to do about it. Present exactly when `textReliability` is `unverified` or `known_issue`. Show it beside the text.
examples: Deleted (struck) language in the source has not yet been checked against this text, so it may read as enacted law. Do not rely on this text without checking the printed act.
notice.title: Notice

officialUrl.description: The publisher's page for this act (never a Vaquill URL): the legislature's page for the bill where it keeps one, else `sourceUrl`. See the same field on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.
officialUrl.title: Officialurl

pageEnd.description: Character offset just past this page. A page is about 30,000 characters, cut back to a paragraph break where one is near, so the length varies.
pageEnd.title: Pageend

pagePrice.description: Credits charged for the page in this response, the same as `creditsConsumed` on this route: the price of one page when a page was served, 0 when none was (`available` is false). Each further page costs the same.
pagePrice.title: Pageprice

pageStart.description: Character offset in the full text where this page starts (0-based). Pages are contiguous: the next page's `pageStart` equals this page's `pageEnd`.
pageStart.title: Pagestart

processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.
processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems

reason.description: Why `available` is false: `not_held`, `withheld`, `pending` or `empty_text`. Null when the text is served.

reasonCode.description: Present when the text is not `verified`, or when `includeUnverified=true` refuses it: a stable token, one of `markup_unverified`, `strike_unchecked`, `struck_text_shown_as_current`, `struck_text_merged`, `veto_unchecked`, `licence_unconfirmed`, `markup_contradicted`, `struck_text_evidenced`, `markup_lost`, `strike_unconfirmed` (the text is served with a flag) or `validation_failed`, `session_unresolved`, `collector_unaudited`, `licence_barred`, `unclassified` (the text is not served). The sentence in `withheldReason` is for people; branch on this.

session.description: The legislative session the law was enacted in.

sessionLawId.description: The law this page belongs to.

sourceUrl.description: The official page or file this text was collected from, on a government publisher's host. Present on EVERY outcome, a withheld or not-held law included, so a reader is never at a dead end: where we do not serve the text, this is where to read it. Null only when we hold no government text source for the law.
sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl

text.description: This page of the act's text, exactly as printed, in reading order. Concatenating every page's `text` in order reproduces the whole text. Where `amendatoryMarkup` is `preserved`, struck and inserted language is in the text in the convention `markupConvention` names. Null when `available` is false.
examples:
CHAPTER 1--S.F.No. 1552

An act

relating to agriculture; ...

textReliability.description: How far to trust this text. Present when you sent `includeUnverified=true`, and on every read whose text is not `verified`. `verified`: the text passed our strike-through check. `unverified`: a check has not been completed, so the text MAY show deleted or vetoed law as if enacted. `known_issue`: we have evidence it does. A served law can be any of the three and its text is served either way. Branch on `reasonCode`, show `notice`.
textReliability.title: Textreliability

textSha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the full text of this law. It changes only when the text does, so it is the cheap way to tell whether a copy you hold is current. Body pages carry the same value.

textStatus.description: Whether we serve this law's text. `held`: the text is served by `/us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`. `withheld`: we hold the text but a measured defect keeps it from being served, and `withheldReason` says what. `not_held`: we know the act exists and do not hold its text. `pending`: collected and not yet verified.

totalChars.description: Length of the whole text in characters. This page is the last when `pageEnd` equals it.

totalPages.description: The most pages the whole text can take: a page holds up to the page size but is cut back to a paragraph break, so every page but the last is counted at its shortest size. A long act usually takes fewer pages and never more. Null when no text is served.

withheldReason.description: Present only when `textStatus` is `withheld`: what is wrong with the text we hold. A plain sentence to show, not an enum to branch on.

SessionLawDetailSession.description: The session block of a single law: the session, and whether we hold all of it.

code.description: Session code, `{year}{type}{ordinal}`. `type` is `R` regular, `S` special, `X` extraordinary, `F` fiscal, `V` veto, `U` unknown. A regular session has no ordinal (`2025R`); a numbered special session carries it (`2025S1`, the first special session of 2025); a lettered one carries its letter (`2025SC`, Florida's Special Session C). `year` is the year the publisher numbers the session by, which for a period spanning two years is the first (District of Columbia Council Period 25 is `2023R`). Pass it as `session` to `GET /us/session-laws/list`.
code.title: Code

coverageStatus.description: Whether we hold every law of this session. `complete`: every law the publisher lists for the session is accounted for, so a law absent from the list does not exist. `partial`: the collection of the session stopped short, so a law that is not found may exist, and this law's neighbours may be missing. The same verdict, with the counts behind it, is in the `sessionLaws` block on `GET /us/statutes/coverage`. Omitted when it cannot be read.
coverageStatus.title: Coveragestatus

label.description: The session's canonical label, as the publisher names it.
label.title: Label

year.description: The year the session convened, the same year `code` starts with.
year.title: Year

SessionLawDetailSession.title: SessionLawDetailSession

SessionLawJurisdictionCoverage.description: A jurisdiction's state session laws (acts as enacted), by session.

completeSessionCount.description: How many of those sessions are `complete`.
completeSessionCount.title: Completesessioncount

earliestApprovedDate.description: The earliest approval date among this jurisdiction's session laws, ISO 8601: the start of what the approval-date filters on `GET /us/session-laws/list` can match. Omitted when no law prints an approval date or the span cannot be read.
earliestApprovedDate.title: Earliestapproveddate

instrumentTypes.description: The kinds of measure we hold for this jurisdiction: the values `instrumentType` accepts on `GET /us/session-laws/list`. Omitted when it cannot be read.
instrumentTypes.title: Instrumenttypes

latestApprovedDate.description: The latest approval date among this jurisdiction's session laws, ISO 8601: the end of what the approval-date filters on `GET /us/session-laws/list` can match. Omitted when no law prints an approval date or the span cannot be read.
latestApprovedDate.title: Latestapproveddate

series.description: The numbering series that exist among this jurisdiction's session laws: the values `series` accepts on `GET /us/session-laws/list`. `general` is the ordinary chapter sequence. Omitted when it cannot be read, which is not the same as no series existing.
series.title: Series

servedCount.description: Laws served across every session listed.
servedCount.title: Servedcount

sessionCount.description: Sessions of this jurisdiction we hold session laws for.
sessionCount.title: Sessioncount

denominator.derivation: The publisher's complete listing of this session names 296 measures. We hold 43 of them; the rest are not yet collected.

SessionLawJurisdictionCoverage.title: SessionLawJurisdictionCoverage

SessionLawListCoverage.description: What we hold of the session or state an EMPTY page was asked about.

jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

message.description: One sentence saying what this empty page means and whether it was charged. Free text to show, not an enum to branch on: branch on `status`.
examples: No law in this session matches your filters. We hold every law the publisher lists for 2025R, so this is not a gap in our collection.
message.title: Message

partialSessions.description: Session codes of this state whose collection is `partial`: the ones an empty page may be missing laws from. At most the 10 newest are listed, oldest first, and `message` says how many earlier ones are left out. Empty when none.
partialSessions.title: Partialsessions

reason.description: Present on `not_held`: why we hold nothing, in one plain sentence. A gap in our collection, not a statement that the state enacted no laws.
examples: We have not collected this jurisdiction's session laws yet.
reason.title: Reason

scope.description: `session` when the request named a `session`, `jurisdiction` when it named only the state.
scope.title: Scope

session.description: The session you named, when `scope` is `session` and we hold any of it. Its counts are in the jurisdiction's `sessionLaws` block on `GET /us/statutes/coverage`.

sessionsHeld.description: How many sessions of this state we hold session laws for. 0 when `not_held`.
sessionsHeld.title: Sessionsheld

status.description: `filter_unavailable`: the data cannot satisfy a date filter you sent (see `unavailableFilters`): no law of this state or session carries that kind of date, so the empty page says nothing about the law; not charged. `complete`: we hold every law the publisher lists for what you asked about, so an empty page means nothing matches your filters, and it is charged. `partial`: the collection stopped short, so the empty page may be a gap in our collection and not an absence of law; it is not charged when everything you asked about is partial. On a state-wide request (`scope: jurisdiction`) with some sessions complete and some partial the status is `partial`, `partialSessions` names the ones to doubt, and the page is charged, because for the complete sessions it is a true negative. `not_held`: we hold no session laws for this session or state at all; not charged.
status.title: Status

unavailableFilters.description: The date filters you sent that no law of the state (or of the `session` you named) can satisfy because none carries that date: any of `approvedFrom`, `approvedTo`, `effectiveFrom`, `effectiveTo`. Empty unless `status` is `filter_unavailable` (or `not_held`, which also names them). Drop them: the other filters still work.
unavailableFilters.title: Unavailablefilters

SessionLawListCoverage.title: SessionLawListCoverage

count.description: Rows on this page. Never a total: the list is paged by cursor and has no corpus-wide count.
count.title: Count

coverage.description: Present only on an EMPTY page: what we hold of the session (or state) you asked about, so you can tell `nothing matches your filters` from `we have not collected this`. `status: complete` means the first: the page is charged. `partial` (the collection stopped short) and `not_held` (we hold nothing of it) mean the second: the page is NOT charged and `creditsConsumed` is 0. Omitted when the coverage cannot be read, in which case the empty page is charged as before.

creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price. It includes the `/us/statutes/resolve` fee when a citation was sent where an id goes. 0 when the call was not charged or was refunded (a body that answers `available: false`).
creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed

hasMore.description: True when another page follows. Each page is charged, an empty one included, except an empty page that `coverage` reports as a gap in our collection.
hasMore.title: Hasmore

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page: send it as `cursor`, with the same filters. Null on the last page.
nextCursor.title: Nextcursor

processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.
processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems

results.description: The page of laws, by `session.code` and then `sessionLawId`, both as text in the database's collation, not chapter order (so `..._C10` comes before `..._C2`; sort by `number` client-side if you need chapter order). The record without its dates list, sources or text: fetch those with `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.
results.title: Results

candidateCount.description: On `ambiguous_citation` and `needs_jurisdiction`, how many laws the citation names in all. Compare it with `len(didYouMean)`: when it is larger, `truncated` is true and the list is a sample, not the full set.
candidateCount.title: Candidatecount

defaultSessionLawId.description: On `ambiguous_citation`, the conventional reading when the registry records one, otherwise null. Informational: it is never served for you.
defaultSessionLawId.title: Defaultsessionlawid

detail.description: Human-readable reason, safe to show a user. Branch on `reason`, not on this string: the wording can change.
examples: Session law not found. No law in the registry carries this id. Take ids from a /us/session-laws/list result, or send the citation in its place.
detail.title: Detail

didYouMean.description: Real `sessionLawId`s the input points at: the one that exists in a different case, or every law an ambiguous citation names (at most 20, the conventional reading first). Empty when nothing matched.
didYouMean.title: Didyoumean

jurisdictions.description: On `needs_jurisdiction`, every state (lower-case postal code) where the citation you sent exists. Name one of them in the citation and send it again. Absent on every other reason.
jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions

reason.description: `not_in_registry`: no law carries this id. `wrong_case`: it exists in another letter case, see `didYouMean`. `unresolved_citation`: you sent a citation and no law carries it. `ambiguous_citation`: the citation names several laws, all in `didYouMean`, none chosen for you; `defaultSessionLawId` is the publisher's conventional reading when one is recorded. `federal_session_law`: federal acts are served by /us/statutes/section. `missing_session_law_id`: the URL names an endpoint where the id goes. `needs_jurisdiction`: the citation is in a form several states share and names none, so none was chosen for you; `jurisdictions` lists the states where it exists and `didYouMean` one law per state. `session_not_fully_collected`: nothing matched, and the session the id or citation points into is only partly collected, so the law may exist; `sessionCoverage` says how much of the session we hold. The route's price is never charged on a 404; a citation's resolution fee is kept on `unresolved_citation`, `ambiguous_citation` and `needs_jurisdiction`, and refunded on `session_not_fully_collected`: a miss in a partly collected session is never charged.
reason.title: Reason

sessionCoverage.description: On `session_not_fully_collected`, the partly collected session the id or citation points into: how many laws we hold of how many it is expected to have (`denominator`), and how many are still open. Absent on every other reason. The same block is in `sessionLaws.sessions` on `GET /us/statutes/coverage`.
