When your citation named a supported container (a regulation series, constitution article, Indiana chapter or Illinois article) or several sections, the section served is the FIRST of them and `matchLevel` says so, as on `GET /us/statutes/resolve`.

returned.description: How many citing sections this page returned (the size of `citers`).
returned.title: Returned

total.description: How many distinct sections cite this one across all pages, the same number as `totalCiters` (a lower bound when `totalCitersIsLowerBound` is true). The size of this page is `returned`.
total.title: Total

totalCiters.description: How many distinct sections cite this one across the scanned result, not just this page. The whole count only when `totalCitersIsLowerBound` is false; otherwise a lower bound, because the scan hit its ceiling.
totalCiters.title: Totalciters

totalCitersIsLowerBound.description: True when `totalCiters` stopped at the scan ceiling and more exist. The ranking then covers only the slice that was read (in storage order), so a citer outside it is missing from every page.
totalCitersIsLowerBound.title: Totalcitersislowerbound

truncated.description: True when more citing sections exist beyond this page. Same as `hasMore`; page on with `nextOffset`.
truncated.title: Truncated

verifiedCiters.description: How many of the leading citers had their own text read and confirmed to name this section. They always come first, so the first `verifiedCiters` rows across all pages are confirmed; the rest are listed in the cross-reference index but their text was not read (only the best-ranked candidates are read). A section whose text was read and does not name this one is dropped, never listed.
verifiedCiters.title: Verifiedciters

StatuteCountRequest.description:
Section count for a scope, or for a Boolean expression within it. See `POST /us/statutes/count`.

A natural-language `query` is still refused: ranking runs over a bounded
window, so "how many sections match this question" has no honest answer
beyond the window size. A Boolean expression is different: membership is
a yes or no per section, and the candidate index counts it
(`matchType: "boolean"`, the same expression `/search` would page through).

actStatus.description: Count only sections carrying this status.
actStatus.title: Actstatus

article.description: Article label (`Amendment XIV`) on CONSTITUTION / STATE_CONSTITUTION, or article number (`2-A`) on a STATE / REGULATION code divided by article. Same values and pairing rules as `article` on `/search`.
article.title: Article

code.description: State code identifier, e.g. `tx_26`. With `corpusType=FEDERAL_RULES`, a rule set instead (`frcp`, `uscapp_t28a_fre`). Same values and checks as `code` on `/search`.
code.title: Code

corpusType.description: Corpus to count, single or list. Omit to count every corpus.
corpusType.title: Corpustype

excludeRepealed.description: Exclude sections whose status is affirmatively dead. A section with no recorded status is KEPT, because a missing status is not evidence of repeal. The US Code is served from a stored annual edition, so a section repealed after it closed is counted here; see the same field on `/search` for the measurement.
excludeRepealed.title: Excluderepealed

matchType.description: `"boolean"` to count the sections satisfying `query`. Required with `query`.
matchType.title: Matchtype

query.description: A Boolean expression to count, with `matchType: "boolean"` (same syntax as `/us/statutes/search`). Omit to count the whole scope. A natural-language query cannot be counted: rank it with `/us/statutes/search`.
query.title: Query

state.description: Two-letter jurisdiction code or `federal`, single or list.
state.title: State

StatuteCountRequest.title: StatuteCountRequest

count.description: Sections in scope. This is a SECTION count, not a passage count: long sections are stored as several passages and are counted once.
count.title: Count

creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call.

isExact.description: True when the figure is an exact count. Always true for a scope. StatuteResolveBatchItem.description:
One citation's verdict inside a batch response.

Deliberately the same field names as `StatuteResolveResponse` minus the
per-request bookkeeping, so a caller migrating from the single route reads
each item with the code it already has.

candidates.description: Present only with `missReason: ambiguous_jurisdiction`, and only when we can name the held sections the citation could mean (an acronym two states print, such as `CCR`). At most 10 entries. Pass the right one's `state` to `GET /us/statutes/resolve` to resolve it. Never a pick: when several are listed, none is the answer.
candidates.title: Candidates

citationOutsideFilters.description: Set only when `resolved` is false because the batch's `state` or `corpusType` scope excludes a section this citation DOES name, e.g. a federal citation under `state: ca`. The scope is a constraint, so the verdict stays `resolved: false`; this says why. Retry without the scope named in `excludedBy` to resolve it. No extra charge.

citedSections.title: Citedsections

container.description: Set with `matchLevel: container`. What you cited and the sections inside it; `section` is the first of them. Also set with `matchLevel: multiple` when the citation fits several held sections and none is the one cited (kind `alternatives`): every candidate is listed, `section` is only the first offered. Omitted from the response when it has no value.

inputCitation.description: The citation string you asked to resolve, echoed back.
inputCitation.title: Inputcitation

matchLevel.description: Present only when `section` is NOT the exact unit you cited. `container`: you cited a container in one of the supported forms (a Missouri, New Jersey, West Virginia or Wyoming regulation series or chapter, a constitution article or amendment, an Indiana chapter, an Illinois article, or a U.S. Code chapter such as `18 U.S.C. ch. 96`; a U.S. Code subchapter is not read), and `section` is the FIRST section inside it (see `container` for how many there are and what they are). A state STATUTE chapter, subchapter, title, article or part cited with its container word and a code name we read for that state (`8 Del. C. ch. 1, subch. VII`, `Tex. Penal Code ch. 19`, `N.Y. Penal Law art. 125`, `Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93A`, `La. R.S. Title 14`) also answers `container`, with `section` the first live section in statutory order, but only where we hold that container and its number is unique within the code. A container we do not hold, a missing or unrecognised code name, a regulation or rule set, or a number that repeats in the code (California repeats chapter numbers across its titles) when the citation names more than one level, returns `resolved: false` with `missReason: container_not_supported`. An article that IS the section unit (`La. Civ. Code art. 2315`, `Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 38.23`) is read as a section. To browse chapters, titles and articles use `GET /us/statutes/divisions`. `multiple`: you cited several sections (`§§ 8, 10`, `§§ 1983-1985`) and `section` is the first of them (see `citedSections`), or your citation fits more than one held section (`D.C.COLO.LR 7.1` is both Local Civil and Local Criminal Rule 7.1) and every candidate is listed in `container`; a state statute container number that repeats within its code (`Cal. Penal Code tit. 8` is a title of each of four parts) lists each candidate container's first section there, never picking one, when there are at most 10. `repaired`: the code name you wrote is a recognised miscite and `section` is the one it names (see `repair`); or (`repair.kind: prior_edition`) the text you cited has been replaced by a current one, and `section` is NOT the text you cited: a C.F.R. or U.S.C. section the current code no longer holds, answered with the MOST RECENT historical annual edition we hold, or a superseded rule set whose rule numbers were kept, answered with the current rule (`Tex. R. Civ. Evid. 803` is answered by `Tex. R. Evid. 803`), or a state regulation we hold only as superseded filings, answered with the latest filing (`W. Va. Code R. § 64-14-5`); `repair.interpretedAs` names what was served and why, and `repair.alternatives` lists the other held editions, if any; or (`repair.kind: former_law`, `former_number`) you cited a FORMER section number, recodified or renumbered since, and `section` is the successor the state's own disposition table or history line names, never the former text (a former section split into several answers `multiple`, every successor in `citedSections`). or (`repair.kind: code_name_inferred`) your citation named no code (`CODE ANN. § 73.001`, `Code 4121-3-34`) and `section` is the only one in the state that carries that number, so the code was inferred from the number and not read from your citation; or (`repair.kind: repealed_range`, `renumbered_range`, `range_member`) you cited a New York or California section the publisher printed only inside a run of sections (`6 NYCRR 420.4` inside `420.3 to 420.4`), and `section` is that stub, not the section's own text (`repair.interpretedAs` names the range); `register_reference`: you cited a state register page, and `section` is a rule whose history cites it (see `registerReference`). `resolved` keeps its meaning (a section was returned) and is true at every level; read `matchLevel` to tell an exact section from a first-of-several. Absent for an exact match.
matchLevel.title: Matchlevel

matchedCorpus.description: Present only when the citation names a STATE session law (an act as enacted, for example `CHAPTER 2025-12` or `S.F.No. 1552`) rather than a code section. `resolved` stays false and `section` stays null, because both describe a code section; the law is in `sessionLaw`.
matchedCorpus.title: Matchedcorpus

missReason.description: Present only when `resolved` is false and none of `citationOutsideFilters` / `sessionLaw` already explains it. WHY the citation did not resolve: `ambiguous_jurisdiction` (the form is one several jurisdictions print, or names none, and no `state` was given: pass `state`; `candidates` lists the held sections it could mean when we can name them, and never picks one), `out_of_scope_corpus` (it names a body of law this route does not serve; `missReasonHint` says which and where to look), `former_law` (it names a repealed, renumbered or retired compilation we do not serve as current law; `missReasonHint` names the successor where one is known), `malformed` (no parser reads it: a docket or database token, a case or treatise citation, a string with no section number, or a subdivision or edition year with no section before it), `container_not_supported` (it cites a chapter, article, title or part, not a section; this route resolves sections, and answers a container only in the forms `matchLevel: container` lists: browse it with `GET /us/statutes/divisions`, or cite a section inside it), `not_held` (it reads as a citation to a jurisdiction and corpus we serve, and that corpus does not hold the section), `index_warming` (batch items only: the code this citation names was still being read when the call arrived, so there is NO verdict about the citation; the item is not billed, and sending it again in a few seconds answers it), `lookup_failed` (batch items only: the citation resolved, but WE failed to load or serialize its section, so this says nothing about whether the section exists; the item is refunded and counted in the response's `failedCount`, and retrying it answers it). `miss_reason_unavailable` (the check that explains a miss timed out or failed on our side, so this response carries NO explanation: it says nothing about why the citation did not resolve, and resending it usually answers; the citation's own verdict, unresolved, is unchanged and charged as any miss is). A miss is still charged, because the verdict is the product, except `index_warming` and `lookup_failed`, which are not verdicts and are never charged; the reason itself adds no charge. Absent on a resolved citation.
missReason.title: Missreason

missReasonHint.description: Present with `missReason`. One sentence on what to try next. Prose for a human or an agent; do not parse it. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
missReasonHint.title: Missreasonhint

pinpoint.description: Present only when the citation carried a pinpoint (`625 ILCS 5/11-601(c)`). The unit it names, located inside `section`, so `(c)` returns subsection (c) and not the whole section. The subsection a pinpoint names, located inside the returned section. ALWAYS read `matched` (or `matchLevel`) before using `text` or `fullText`: when the section has no such subsection the block says so rather than staying silent, and under `matchLevel: ancestor` the text fields describe the deepest unit that DOES exist (read `unmatched` for the part of your pinpoint that did not). `path` is the machine form of the pinpoint, one entry per level. `(f)(1.5)` is `["f", "1.5"]` and `(d-1)` is `["d-1"]`, so a label that contains a dot or a hyphen is never split. `text` is the unit's own text (its lead-in when it has children), `fullText` is the unit with everything beneath it exactly as printed, and `leadIn` is each ancestor's own text in order, so a deeply nested unit can be read as the sentence it completes. `charStart` / `charEnd` index into the `plain` text of `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}/body` (see `structure.textSha256`). No extra charge.

pinpointNote.description: Present only when the citation carried a pinpoint and we could not look it up this time (the section text was unavailable, or the lookup failed or ran out of time). The section itself resolved and is charged as usual; `subsection` still echoes the pinpoint. Retrying usually answers.
pinpointNote.title: Pinpointnote

registerReference.description: Present only when `matchLevel` is `register_reference`: the citation names a page, issue or filing of a state register or bulletin. When `registerItemHeld` is true `section` IS that register item (corpusType STATE_REGISTER, a notice as printed, not codified law). Otherwise the item is not held and `section` is a RULE whose history note cites it (the first of `ruleCount`, in document order); read `rules` for the others.

repair.description: Set with `matchLevel: repaired`. The miscite we corrected and how we read it. Omitted from the response when it has no value.

resolved.description: True when this citation resolved to an exact section.
resolved.title: Resolved

section.description: The resolved section, or null when this citation did not resolve.

sessionLaw.description: The state session law this citation names, when it names no code section. `status` is `matched` (one law, read it at `href`) or `ambiguous` (several, all in `candidates`, none chosen for you). Absent when the citation resolved to a section, and whenever session laws cannot be checked. No extra charge.

subsection.description: Parsed pinpoint subsection when the citation carried one. See the single-citation route for the full semantics, including the case where the publisher issues a larger unit than the citation names.
subsection.title: Subsection

StatuteResolveBatchRequest.description:
Batch citation resolution. See `POST /us/statutes/resolve`.

`/resolve` took 1,159 calls in the 16 days to 2026-08-31, second only to
search, and every one of them carried a single citation. The caller shape it
is actually serving is an agent handed a brief, a memo or a model's output
with thirty citations in it, doing thirty round trips to check them.

citations.description:
Bluebook citation strings to resolve. Duplicates are collapsed FIRST and order is preserved, so the response's `results` array lines up with the de-duplicated input.

The cap is 50 UNIQUE citations, applied after that collapse, so a brief quoting one section sixty times is one citation and is accepted.

Priced PER CITATION at the single-resolve rate, exactly like `POST /us/statutes/sections`: batching is a round-trip and latency win, not a discount. Thirty citations cost the same 60 credits either way and take one request instead of thirty.

Same semantics as the single-citation route.

state.description: Optional jurisdiction to resolve every citation WITHIN: a two-letter state code, or `federal` for the U.S. Code, the C.F.R., federal rules and the U.S. Constitution. Applies to the whole batch: a batch spanning jurisdictions should omit it and let each citation name its own. Same semantics as the single-citation route -- a constraint, not a hint.

missReasonHint.description: Present with `missReason`. One sentence on what to try next. Prose for a human or an agent; do not parse it. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
missReasonHint.title: Missreasonhint

pinpoint.description: Present only when the citation carried a pinpoint (`625 ILCS 5/11-601(c)`). The unit it names, located inside `section`, so `(c)` returns subsection (c) and not the whole section. The subsection a pinpoint names, located inside the returned section. ALWAYS read `matched` (or `matchLevel`) before using `text` or `fullText`: when the section has no such subsection the block says so rather than staying silent, and under `matchLevel: ancestor` the text fields describe the deepest unit that DOES exist (read `unmatched` for the part of your pinpoint that did not). `path` is the machine form of the pinpoint, one entry per level. `(f)(1.5)` is `["f", "1.5"]` and `(d-1)` is `["d-1"]`, so a label that contains a dot or a hyphen is never split. `text` is the unit's own text (its lead-in when it has children), `fullText` is the unit with everything beneath it exactly as printed, and `leadIn` is each ancestor's own text in order, so a deeply nested unit can be read as the sentence it completes. `charStart` / `charEnd` index into the `plain` text of `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}/body` (see `structure.textSha256`). No extra charge.

pinpointNote.description: Present only when the citation carried a pinpoint and we could not look it up this time (the section text was unavailable, or the lookup failed or ran out of time). The section itself resolved and is charged as usual; `subsection` still echoes the pinpoint. Retrying usually answers.
pinpointNote.title: Pinpointnote

processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Useful for spotting a slow query; not billed on.
processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems

registerReference.description: Present only when `matchLevel` is `register_reference`: the citation names a page, issue or filing of a state register or bulletin. When `registerItemHeld` is true `section` IS that register item (corpusType STATE_REGISTER, a notice as printed, not codified law). Otherwise the item is not held and `section` is a RULE whose history note cites it (the first of `ruleCount`, in document order); read `rules` for the others.

repair.description: Set with `matchLevel: repaired`. The miscite we corrected and how we read it. Omitted from the response when it has no value.

resolved.description: True when the citation resolved to an exact section.
resolved.title: Resolved

section.description: The resolved section, or null when the citation did not resolve.

sessionLaw.description: The state session law this citation names, when it names no code section. `status` is `matched` (one law, read it at `href`) or `ambiguous` (several, all in `candidates`, none chosen for you). Absent when the citation resolved to a section, and whenever session laws cannot be checked. No extra charge.

subsection.description: Parsed pinpoint subsection when the citation carried one, e.g. 'b.2' for '42 U.S.C. 1983(b)(2)'. The returned section is the parent. It is also set when the citation names a unit SMALLER than the one the publisher issues: Rhode Island cites a regulation by section ('250-RICR-120-05-15.2') but publishes the whole Part, so `section` is Part 15 and `subsection` is '15.2'. A non-null `subsection` always means `section` is the containing document, not the exact unit you cited. The string is dot-joined, so `(f)(1.5)` reads `f.1.5`: read `pinpoint` for the unit itself, with a machine-safe `path`.
subsection.title: Subsection

StatuteResult.description: A single statute section from search results.

abstract.description: The issuing agency's own summary of the document, as published in the Federal Register. Populated on 99.9% of rules and proposed rules, so a document can be triaged without fetching the full text. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
examples: This regulation extends time-limited tolerances for pesticides.
abstract.title: Abstract

actStatus.description: Raw section status: `in_force`, `repealed`, `renumbered`, `transferred`, `omitted`, `reserved`, `vacant`, or `unconstitutional`. Some corpora also use `superseded` (a prior version), `enacted`, `pending` and `non_precedential`. This is the status recorded for the section; the currency verdict is `goodLawStatus`. Always present; null when not known.
actStatus.title: Actstatus

action.description: The Federal Register's own ACTION line, ~100% populated. Carries distinctions no other field makes: interim final rule, direct final rule, withdrawal, reopening of the comment period. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
action.title: Action

adoptedAfterCurrentThrough.description: New York only. True when `pendingAdoptions` is non-empty, i.e. the State Register records at least one adoption naming this section or its Part that post-dates the volume `currentThrough` refers to, so the text served may be out of date. Null (never false) when no such adoption is recorded; null is not a claim that the text is current. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
adoptedAfterCurrentThrough.title: Adoptedaftercurrentthrough

adoptingCitations.description:
Citations to the instrument that ADOPTED this rule: the state register notice, the Washington filing number, the adopting order. The rulemaking audit trail.

Unified across four different payload spellings, so this is comparable across states in a way the underlying data is not.

These are also the independent way to confirm a section when the publisher's own page cannot be read without a browser (see `externalUrl`): a Texas rule's `['50 TexReg 8285']` names the Texas Register issue and page that printed its adoption. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
adoptingCitations.title: Adoptingcitations

agencies.description: Issuing agencies, by name. Populated on 99.9% of Federal Register documents. Pair with `agencySlugs` when you need the token the `agency` search filter takes. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
agencies.title: Agencies

agencySlugs.description: The issuing agencies as slugs. These are exactly the values the `agency` filter on `/us/statutes/search` accepts, so an agency facet can be round-tripped straight back into a query. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
agencySlugs.title: Agencyslugs

alternateCitations.description:
Other official citation forms for THIS document, where a publisher prints more than one. Puerto Rico gives an L.P.R.A. cite, Arizona a long form, the IRS an Internal Revenue Bulletin cite, the Federal Reserve a paired Consumer Affairs number.

Distinct from `relatedCitations`, which is what this document points AT. Use these when you need to match a citation a user typed in the form their jurisdiction actually publishes. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
alternateCitations.title: Alternatecitations

amendmentHistory.description: Structured amendment entries where the publisher records them separately from the credit line in `history`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
amendmentHistory.title: Amendmenthistory

amendmentHistoryNote.description: Present only when the section carries no amendment evidence and its state or document type does not record enough amendment history to read absence as a fact (for example New York, Massachusetts, Arizona and West Virginia statutes, several states' regulations, court rules and constitutions, opinions, register notices, bulletins, annual CFR editions and session laws). It says `amendmentYears`, `lastAmendedYear` and `amendmentsCount` are absent because nothing was recorded, not because the section is unamended; `amendmentsCount` is then null rather than 0. Also present on a Maryland section whose `history` is generated from General Assembly session data rather than a publisher credit line. Null where history is recorded, and an empty history there does mean the section has not been amended.
amendmentHistoryNote.title: Amendmenthistorynote

amendmentNote.description: The publisher's amendment credit line where it is stored separately from `history`. Illinois and Colorado regulations, ~72% populated. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
examples: Amended at 37 Ill. Reg. 16539, effective October 4, 2013
amendmentNote.title: Amendmentnote

amendmentYears.description:
Distinct years the section was amended, parsed from the publisher's history note.

Always newest first, and de-duplicated. Ingesters store the array in both orders (eCFR writes newest first, state regulations and state statutes write oldest first), so the order is imposed at serve time and the served order is the only one to rely on. Years outside 1789..(current year) are dropped rather than served: amendment dates are parsed out of prose and a note can yield a sunset or substitution date that is not an amendment at all. Always present; null when not known.
amendmentYears.title: Amendmentyears

amendmentsCount.description:
How many amendments the publisher recorded for this section. Not the length of `amendmentYears`, and it is not safe to derive one from the other.

For regulations and court rules this counts amending EVENTS: one per register citation, filing or history entry, so a section amended twice in the same year counts 2 against a single entry in `amendmentYears`. The two disagree on a large share of the regulation and court-rule corpora, so read each for what it is. For the other corpora, and for any source that publishes no per-event record, it is the number of distinct years and is capped at the length of `amendmentYears`, so it never counts a year the list dropped as implausible; it understates a section amended twice in one year. Always present; null when not known.
amendmentsCount.title: Amendmentscount

articleName.description: Article title, the companion to `articleNumber`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
articleName.title: Articlename

articleNumber.description: Article number. Article is the PRIMARY hierarchy level in state constitutions, where `chapter` and `part` are 0-6% populated, so without this those corpora served almost no structure. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
articleNumber.title: Articlenumber

audience.description: Who the document is addressed to or binds, where the issuer states it. 100% populated on the Montana insurance bulletins. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
audience.title: Audience

body.description:
Full plain text of the section. Always a key on the row: filled only when the request set `includeBody: true`, and null otherwise and on any row whose text could not be resolved (those rows are not charged for a body). A section the publisher prints as images has no text: its `body` is null and `bodyUnavailable` is `true`.

This is the actual statutory text, not the `excerpt`. The two are different things and the difference matters for quoting: `excerpt` is a ranking preview windowed around the match, so it can begin mid-section and drop a leading subsection marker -- measured 2026-09-02, four of five California rows lost their opening `(a) `. `body` is the document as the publisher printed it.
examples: (a) If within a reasonable time after written or oral notice...
body.title: Body

bodyNote.description: Present only when the request set `includeBody: true` and this row's `body` is null for a reason on our side or yours, so a null body is never silent. `fetch_failed`: reading the text failed this time, retry; not charged. `no_text`: the read succeeded but returned no text for this section; not charged. `insufficient_credits`: your balance could not cover the bodies, so every body on the page was withheld (the ranking you paid for is intact); top up and repeat the call. `response_size_cap`: a batch response carries at most 4,000,000 characters of inline body text, and this row's body was dropped to stay under it; not charged, fetch it from `/section/{actId}/body`. A section printed as images carries `bodyUnavailable` instead.
bodyNote.title: Bodynote

bodyServedNote.description: Present only when the request set `includeBody: true` and the `body` on this row is not the section's preferred copy: a lesser copy was served because the preferred one could not be read this time, a rendered table or figure was withheld, or the text is partial. The same words `/section/{actId}/body` returns in `note`. Not cached, so a repeat call may return the preferred copy.
bodyServedNote.title: Bodyservednote

bodyUnavailable.description: Present, and `true`, only on a section that has no text to return: the publisher prints it as images (an appendix, a form, a map), or the text we hold is only a partial copy of the official text. Omitted on every other section. The section is real and its metadata is complete; there is simply no body, so `body` / `plain` / `html` are null, `available` is false on `/body`, and nothing is charged for a body. Read it instead of treating a null body as a fetch failure that is worth retrying.
bodyUnavailable.title: Bodyunavailable

bodyUnavailableReason.description: Why there is no body, present with `bodyUnavailable`. `image_only_source`: the publisher prints this section as images, so there is no text to extract. Where we hold an official link for the section it is in `sourceUrl`; it is null where we may not republish the publisher's link. `misfiled_source_text`: the text stored under this regulation opens with another rule's number (a prior version filed under a renumbered rule), so it is withheld rather than served as this rule. `partial_snapshot_text`: the text we hold for this section is only a partial copy of the official text, so it is withheld rather than served as if it were complete. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
bodyUnavailableReason.title: Bodyunavailablereason

breadcrumb.description: Structured breadcrumb trail for navigation. Always present; null when not known.
breadcrumb.title: Breadcrumb

caseName.description: The charged party or covered entity a document concerns. Only 27% equal to `sectionTitle` on HHS OCR, so it is not recoverable from the served text. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
caseName.title: Casename

chapter.description: Chapter number or identifier. Always present; null when not known.
chapter.title: Chapter

chapterName.description: Chapter name. Always present; null when not known.
chapterName.title: Chaptername

citation.description: Full citation (e.g., '42 U.S.C. § 1983 (2024)', '17 C.F.R. § 240.10b5-1 (2026)'). Always present; null when not known.
citation.title: Citation

citationNote.description: Present only on a state-constitution unit the source gives no section number (an amendment, preamble, schedule or whole article). `citation` is then the article-level form without a section sign, and `sectionNumber` is null. Absent otherwise.
citationNote.title: Citationnote

citationShort.description: Short citation (e.g., '42 U.S.C. § 1983', '17 C.F.R. § 240.10b5-1'). Always present; null when not known.
citationShort.title: Citationshort

committeeNote.description: Advisory-committee note on a procedural rule: the standard interpretive gloss courts read alongside the rule text. Deliberately separate from `amendmentNote`, which records when the rule changed rather than what it means. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
committeeNote.title: Committeenote

corpusType.description: The corpus this section belongs to: one of `USC`, `CFR`, `STATE`, `CONSTITUTION`, `FEDERAL_RULES`, `FEDERAL_LOCAL_RULES`, `STATE_CONSTITUTION`, `STATE_RULES`, `EXECUTIVE_ACTION`, `REGULATION`, `FEDERAL_REGISTER`, `FEDERAL_REGISTER_NOTICE`, `AGENCY_GUIDANCE`, `SENTENCING_GUIDELINES`, `US_TAX_TREATY`, `US_TREATY`, `STATE_AGENCY_GUIDANCE`, `STATE_AG_OPINION`, `STATE_REGISTER`, `SESSION_LAW`, `STATUTE_COMPILATION`, `AGENCY_ADJUDICATION`, `CFR_ANNUAL`, `USC_ANNUAL`, `FEDERAL_BILL`, `FEDERAL_RULES_ANNUAL`, `FEDERAL_RULES_PROPOSED`. The same tokens the `corpusType` filter accepts. Always present; null when not known.
corpusType.title: Corpustype

court.description: The body that heard the matter, where the publisher names one. Distinct from `forum`, which is the KIND of proceeding: `forum` has two values and is what you filter on, `court` has as many values as there are districts and is for display. Populated on every CFPB civil action and on the administrative proceedings the Bureau labels with its own adjudication office. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
examples: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts
court.title: Court

crossReferencesCfr.description: CFR cross-references parsed from the text, e.g. `['1.6011-4']`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
crossReferencesCfr.title: Crossreferencescfr

crossReferencesCfrChecked.description: Each distinct entry of `crossReferencesCfr`, checked against the sections we hold. Only populated on `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}` for a CFR section with references; null on search results and when the check could not be made, in which case treat the raw list as unchecked. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
crossReferencesCfrChecked.title: Crossreferencescfrchecked

crossReferencesUsc.description: USC cross-references parsed from the text, e.g. `['42:1983']`. `'self:<section>'` denotes a reference to another section of the same title. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
crossReferencesUsc.title: Crossreferencesusc

currencyNote.description: Source's 'current through ...' note, when published. Always present; null when not known.
currencyNote.title: Currencynote

currencyYear.description: Machine-readable counterpart to `currencyNote`, which is prose. 100% populated on the nine state-regulation corpora that carry a currency statement. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
currencyYear.title: Currencyyear

currentThrough.description: How current the publisher says this text is, in the publisher's own terms. A date (`2025-01-06`) on every USC section and most compilations; otherwise the publisher's wording (`Current through Act 9046 of the 2025 session`, `Public Law 119-60`, `Supp. 19-2`, `2024 Edition`). Do not parse it as a date without checking its shape. `currencyNote` carries the same fact as prose where a publisher writes it that way. Always present; null when not known.
currentThrough.title: Currentthrough

datesText.description: The verbatim DATES block from the Federal Register, ~98% populated. Worth reading alongside `frEffectiveOn`: a rule with staged or conditional effective dates has them here, and the single date flattens that away. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
datesText.title: Datestext

displayLabel.description:
The publisher's own short label for this section, e.g. `Cal. BPC § 655.2` or `MPEP § 2165.03`. Populated on essentially every document we hold.

Usually equal to `citationShort`, but not always: on the Federal Communications Commission, NLRB, HHS OCR and BIS corpora the two differ on every document, and there `displayLabel` is the form the publisher itself prints. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
displayLabel.title: Displaylabel

displayPath.description: Full hierarchical path (Title > Chapter > Section). Always present; null when not known.
displayPath.title: Displaypath

documentNumber.description: The issuer's own document or case number, for exact lookup: an FCC DA number, an NLRB case-handling docket, a ruling number. On NLRB advice memoranda and FCC/HHS OCR documents this is not recoverable from `sectionNumber`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
documentNumber.title: Documentnumber

documentSubtype.description: Finer instrument class where the publisher gives one. On presidential documents this separates an executive order from a proclamation, a memorandum or a notice (~90% populated there). Omitted from the response when it has no value.
documentSubtype.title: Documentsubtype

documentTypeLabel.description: The instrument type as the publisher names it: `Rule`, `Proposed Rule`, `Presidential Document`, `Declaratory Ruling`, `Resolution Agreement`. Deliberately not `corpusType`, which says which body of law a document belongs to: two documents in one corpus can be very different instruments. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
documentTypeLabel.title: Documenttypelabel

docxUrl.description: Microsoft Word (DOCX) version, when available. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
docxUrl.title: Docxurl

edition.description: The publisher's edition or year for this text. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
edition.title: Edition

effectiveDate.description: When THIS version took effect, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null when the publisher's own string does not name one unambiguous day we can read without guessing. On a section with `actStatus=superseded` this is the start of that version's window. The publisher's wording is preserved in `effectiveDateRaw` whenever it differs.
effectiveDate.title: Effectivedate

effectiveDateRaw.description: The date exactly as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `effectiveDate`. A section whose publisher already prints ISO leaves this null. Expect prose (`September 8, 1916`), abbreviated months (`Feb. 25, 1868`), US numerics (`9/28/15`), Spanish for Puerto Rico (`26 de junio de 1963`), and values that are not a single date at all (`April 1, 2023 to June 30, 2026`), which is why they cannot be published under `effectiveDate`.
effectiveDateRaw.title: Effectivedateraw

executiveOrderNumber.description: The executive order number a lawyer cites the order by (`14179` for Executive Order 14179 of January 23, 2025). Set only on executive orders; the `citation` is the Federal Register page, not this. See `instrumentNumberSource` for where the value came from. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
executiveOrderNumber.title: Executiveordernumber

expirationDate.description: When this rule lapses unless re-adopted, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Distinct from `reviewDate` (the review deadline) and from any amendment date: it is in the future and it ENDS the rule. See `expirationDateRaw` for the publisher's wording. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
expirationDate.title: Expirationdate

expirationDateRaw.description: The expiry date as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `expirationDate`. State regulators print this as `1/1/2028` and `03-01-2029` as well as ISO.
expirationDateRaw.title: Expirationdateraw

externalUrl.description:
The publisher's own page for this section, exactly as recorded at ingest: uscode.house.gov, ecfr.gov, a state legislature or a state register. Null when the publisher issues no per-section link, or when the link is withheld. Prefer `sourceUrl`, which is this link when present and otherwise the best official alternative.

Some official publishers serve their code only through a JavaScript application, so the link renders in a browser but returns an empty page shell to a plain HTTP client. Texas is the main case: the Secretary of State publishes the Texas Administrative Code only on its Appian portal (texas-sos.appianportalsgov.com). The link is still the correct citation. To check a section without a browser, use `adoptingCitations` (for Texas, the `NN TexReg PPPP` register citations that adopted and amended it) and read the text we captured at `textUrl`.
externalUrl.title: Externalurl

federalRegisterCitations.description: Federal Register citations associated with the section, e.g. `['48 FR 3956', '49 FR 15073']`. This is the CFR's form of the credit line `sourceCredit` carries for the USC: the rulemakings that established and amended the section. Populated on 37.4% of CFR sections, empty where eCFR prints no source note. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
federalRegisterCitations.title: Federalregistercitations

fieldAbsenceNote.description: Present only when `year` or `effectiveDate` is null AND the ingester of this whole document type never records it (state constitutions carry no `year`; federal local court rules rarely carry a `year` or `effectiveDate`, as of 2026-10-31). It says the field is null because nothing was recorded, which is not a claim that the document has no such date. Null otherwise.
fieldAbsenceNote.title: Fieldabsencenote

forum.description: For `corpusType=AGENCY_ADJUDICATION`, the KIND of proceeding that produced the document, in the publisher's own words. On CFPB enforcement actions this is `Administrative Proceeding` (the Bureau's own Office of Administrative Adjudication, under 12 C.F.R. Part 1081) or `Civil Action` (a suit the Bureau filed in a federal district court). One action can carry both, in which case they are joined with `; `. Null on every other corpus. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
forum.title: Forum

frCommentsCloseOn.description: Public-comment deadline (ISO 8601 date). Proposed rules only. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frCommentsCloseOn.title: Frcommentscloseon

frCorrectionOf.description: Federal Register document number this document corrects, when this is a correction. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frCorrectionOf.title: Frcorrectionof

frCorrections.description: Federal Register document number(s) that later corrected this document. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frCorrections.title: Frcorrections

frDocketIds.description: Rulemaking docket ID(s) this document was filed under. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frDocketIds.title: Frdocketids

frEffectiveOn.description: The rule's effective date (ISO 8601 date), when set. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frEffectiveOn.title: Freffectiveon

frEndPage.description: Last Federal Register page. With `frStartPage` this gives the page RANGE, which `citation` cannot express because it carries only the first page. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frEndPage.title: Frendpage

frRegulationIdNumbers.description: Regulation Identifier Number(s) (RIN) assigned to this rule. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frRegulationIdNumbers.title: Frregulationidnumbers

frRegulationsDotGovUrl.description: Link to this document's public comment docket on regulations.gov. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frRegulationsDotGovUrl.title: Frregulationsdotgovurl

frRelatedDocuments.description: Other Federal Register documents sharing this document's RIN(s) (its proposed rule, its final rule, and any corrections), most recent first. Only populated on `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}` for a row that carries `frRegulationIdNumbers`; always null on `/us/statutes/search` results, since computing it needs a follow-up lookup that is too expensive to run per search result. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frRelatedDocuments.title: Frrelateddocuments

frRelatedDocumentsNote.description: Set only when `frRelatedDocuments` is absent for a reason you should know: this document's RIN is shared by more than 25 other Federal Register documents (an umbrella RIN), so it names no single rulemaking and listing any subset would be a guess; or the related-document lookup was temporarily unavailable, so the list may be incomplete and a repeat call returns it. In that case the call is refunded (`creditsConsumed` is 0). Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frRelatedDocumentsNote.title: Frrelateddocumentsnote

frSignificant.description: Whether the Federal Register marked this rule 'economically significant' (EO 12866). Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frSignificant.title: Frsignificant

frStartPage.description: First Federal Register page, the `64768` in `66 FR 64768`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frStartPage.title: Frstartpage

frVolume.description: Federal Register volume, the `66` in `66 FR 64768`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
frVolume.title: Frvolume

goodLawBasis.description:
Why `goodLawStatus` has the value it has, as a short code; `null` exactly when `goodLawStatus` is `null`.

`good_law`: `in_force` (recorded in force, in a jurisdiction whose repeal information we track).

`not_good_law`: `repealed_or_moved` (repealed, renumbered, transferred or recodified), `past_edition` (an annual edition later editions supersede), `proposal` (a bill or proposed rule, never law at any stage), `superseded_by_later_guidance` (IRS guidance a later document superseded, obsoleted or revoked in full), `later_rule_removed` (a Federal Register final rule a later final rule removed from the CFR) or `later_order_revoked` (an executive order a later one revokes or supersedes in full). For the last three `supersededBy` names the later document, and for the last `actStatus` reads `revoked` or `superseded`.

`not_operative`: `reserved_or_inactive` (reserved, vacant or unfunded), `not_yet_effective` (a future effective date is printed in the heading, or a final rule's `frEffectiveOn` is ahead) or `publisher_marker` (the publisher's own bracketed note in the heading).

`unknown`: `no_repeal_signal` (the publisher gives no repeal markers to check its stored status against), `frozen_snapshot` (served from an edition frozen at a past date), `stated_as_of_date` (current only to the date the text states), `no_status`, `text_omitted_by_publisher` (the legislature prints only a placeholder such as 'Amendatory provisions; text omitted'; `currencyNote` says so) or `status_unrecognized`.
goodLawBasis.title: Goodlawbasis

goodLawStatus.description: Derived currency verdict: `good_law`, `not_good_law`, `not_operative`, or `unknown`. `unknown` means no currency verdict is asserted for the section, which is different from out of date. It is returned where a jurisdiction does not publish repeal information (state statutes for California, for example, are stored `in_force` with `goodLawStatus: unknown`: the stored status is the publisher's own, and we do not certify it current because that state's repeal markers have not been verified), and for these corpora by design: attorney general opinions, register notices, statute compilations, the U.S. Code, executive actions and treaties. Annual editions (`cfr_annual`, `usc_annual`) return `not_good_law` because a later edition supersedes them. Read `corpusType` beside this field. `null` when currency checking is disabled.
goodLawStatus.title: Goodlawstatus

govInfoHtmlUrl.description: Official govinfo.gov HTML version. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
govInfoHtmlUrl.title: Govinfohtmlurl

govInfoPdfUrl.description: Official govinfo.gov PDF version. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
govInfoPdfUrl.title: Govinfopdfurl

granuleId.description: govinfo granule identifier (USC/CFR provenance). Omitted from the response when it has no value.
granuleId.title: Granuleid

history.description: The publisher's own amendment/history credit line, verbatim, e.g. `Effective 5/4/2005; Superseded 8/1/2016`. `amendmentYears` is parsed from this; keep both when you need the exact wording. Always present; null when not known.
history.title: History

historyEffectiveDate.description: When this version took effect, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, read out of the publisher's amendment credit line in `history`, which is returned beside it as the evidence. A weaker fact than `effectiveDate` (a date the publisher put in a date field), so it is populated only where `effectiveDate` is null. It is the newest commencement the credit line names, and null whenever that cannot be stated without guessing: a credit line that dates only some entries, a date that belongs to a repeal, sunset, applicability rule or another section, a commencement still in the future, a date older than `lastAmendedYear`, or a state whose `history` format we have not measured. Statutes only.
historyEffectiveDate.title: Historyeffectivedate

htmlUrl.description: HTML version of the statute section. Always present; null when not known.
htmlUrl.title: Htmlurl

implementingRegulations.description: For a USC section: the CFR parts that implement it, derived from the reverse of every CFR section's own `statutoryAuthority`, e.g. `[{'cfrTitle': 17, 'part': '240', 'partName': '...', 'display': '17 CFR Part 240'}]`. Null for non-USC corpora. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
implementingRegulations.title: Implementingregulations

instrumentNumberSource.description: Provenance of `executiveOrderNumber` / `proclamationNumber`. `stored` is the number recorded when the document was ingested. `derived_from_text` is read at request time from the document's own header line (`Executive Order 14179 of January 23, 2025`), accepted only when that line opens the document and its date equals `signingDate`; it is null when the header is not in the text returned (for example a later chunk of a search hit), which means unknown, not unnumbered. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
instrumentNumberSource.title: Instrumentnumbersource

issueDate.description: Issue/publication date of this version, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, when known. See `issueDateRaw` for the publisher's wording on the rare source that does not print ISO. Always present; null when not known.
issueDate.title: Issuedate

issueDateRaw.description: The issue date as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `issueDate`. Null across the corpus today; it exists so a source that starts printing prose cannot silently put prose in a field documented as a date.
issueDateRaw.title: Issuedateraw

issuingAgency.description:
The body that promulgated or issued this document: the state agency behind a regulation, the division behind an agency letter.

Populated at 83.6-100% across the state-regulation corpora that carry it. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
issuingAgency.title: Issuingagency

languageCode.description: ISO code of the language the document is written in, present where a corpus is not wholly English. 86% of Puerto Rico insurance bulletins are Spanish (`es`). Omitted from the response when it has no value.
languageCode.title: Languagecode

lastAmendedDate.description: Full date of the most recent amendment, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, where the publisher gives one. See `lastAmendedDateRaw` for the wording. Illinois and Colorado regulations carry their amendment provenance only here and in `amendmentNote`: neither state has a `history`, and Colorado has no `effectiveDate` either, so for Colorado this is the only date that exists. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
lastAmendedDate.title: Lastamendeddate

lastAmendedDateRaw.description: The last-amended date as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `lastAmendedDate`, or null when it is not a date at all.
lastAmendedDateRaw.title: Lastamendeddateraw

lastAmendedYear.description: Most recent amendment year, when known. Re-derived at serve time as `max(amendmentYears)`, so it never exceeds the list served beside it. Falls back to the publisher's own scalar only when `amendmentYears` is empty, and only when that scalar is itself within 1789..(current year). Always present; null when not known.
lastAmendedYear.title: Lastamendedyear

lawImplemented.description: The statute this rule IMPLEMENTS, as distinct from `statutoryAuthority`, which is the statute granting the rulemaking power. Florida populates both and they differ. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
lawImplemented.title: Lawimplemented

matchContexts.description:
Present only with `matchType: "boolean"`: up to 3 passages showing where this section satisfied the expression, in the order they appear in the section. Highlights follow the engine that decides membership: every conjunct of an AND, the OR branches that matched, the words of a phrase, both operands of a satisfied `/N`, `/s` or `/p` pair, the occurrences counted by `atleastN`, and for `a NOT W/N b` the `a` that has no `b` in range. A NOT never highlights anything.

Unlike `excerpt` (the passage the relevance model ranked, which may not contain your terms), these passages always do. Empty (`[]`) when the expression matched only in the heading or citation (`title( )`, `cite( )`). Absent on a row whose passages could not be prepared within the search's time allowance; the row is still a verified match. Contexts never change which sections are returned, their order, or the price.
matchContexts.title: Matchcontexts

matchNoteYear.description: When `matchSegment` is `note`, the year named by the note heading the passage sits under (1993 for 'Notes of Advisory Committee on Rules, 1993 Amendment'). Null when the heading names no year or `matchSegment` is not `note`.
matchNoteYear.title: Matchnoteyear

matchSegment.description: On a search hit in a federal rule, which part of the rule document the matched passage sits in: `rule_text`, `source_credit`, or `note` (an Advisory Committee Note). Null when unknown, and always null outside federal rules and on a section fetched by id. A label only, it never changes the ranking.
matchSegment.title: Matchsegment

originalEnactmentDate.description: When the section was FIRST enacted, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, ~72% populated on the US Code. Deliberately separate from `effectiveDate`: merging them would report an amended section as effective from its original year. On 35.7% of US Code points this is the only enactment date we hold. See `originalEnactmentDateRaw` for the publisher's wording. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
originalEnactmentDate.title: Originalenactmentdate

originalEnactmentDateRaw.description: The enactment date as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `originalEnactmentDate`. The US Code prints `Aug. 14, 1935` where GovInfo statute compilations print `1935-08-14` for the same fact.
originalEnactmentDateRaw.title: Originalenactmentdateraw

packageId.description: govinfo package identifier (USC/CFR provenance). Omitted from the response when it has no value.
packageId.title: Packageid

parent.description: Query for `GET /us/statutes/divisions` that lists this section's siblings (its containing chapter, part, code, article or federal rule set). Pass it straight back to walk up the hierarchy, or spread it into a `POST /us/statutes/search` body to search within that container: every key it carries is also a search filter. Null when the container cannot be determined.
parent.title: Parent

part.description: Part number or identifier (CFR/state). Always present; null when not known.
part.title: Part

partName.description: Part name. Always present; null when not known.
partName.title: Partname

pdfUrl.description: PDF version of the statute section. Always present; null when not known.
pdfUrl.title: Pdfurl

pendingAdoptions.description:
New York only. State Register adoption notices that post-date the print volume this section's text was taken from. They are notices, not an updated consolidated text: `text` and `body` still reflect `currentThrough` / `currencyNote`. Look the notice up in the State Register by its `idNo`.

Each entry: `idNo` (e.g. `DFS-23-26-00013-A`), `scope` (`section` when the notice names this section, `part` when it names the Part containing it), `effectiveDate` (ISO date, null if the notice states none), `agency`, `issueDate` (ISO date of the Register issue). No link is returned; it is withheld under licence, as with `sourceUrl` on these regulations. Only adoptions (`-A`, `-AA`) are listed, never proposals, emergency rules or withdrawals.

Null on every section with no such notice, which does not mean the section is current: we cover Register adoptions for NYCRR Titles 3, 19 and 23 only. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
pendingAdoptions.title: Pendingadoptions

pendingAmendments.description: Federal Rules only: the amendments proposed to this rule that are not yet in force, each with its lifecycle `status`, `cycle`, `effectiveDate`, `commentPeriodEnd`, `sourceUrl` and `textComplete`. Fetch one with `GET /us/statutes/section/{id}`. Absent on every other section and on a rule with nothing pending. A proposal is never law until its effective date: the text above is the rule in force.
pendingAmendments.title: Pendingamendments

popularName.description: Popular/common name of the act (e.g. 'Truth in Lending Act'), when known. Always present; null when not known.
popularName.title: Popularname

president.description: The president in office for this document, on Federal Register and presidential-document corpora spanning 1994 to present. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
president.title: President

priorEffectiveDates.description: Earlier effective dates recorded for the section, each as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the order the publisher lists them. A publisher's list written as one string (`3-15-22; 7-1-26`) is split into its dates. A value that names no single day (`March 2007`, `immediately`) is not here: it is in `priorEffectiveDatesRaw`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
priorEffectiveDates.title: Prioreffectivedates

priorEffectiveDatesRaw.description: The publisher's own wording of `priorEffectiveDates`, one string per stored entry, present only when it differs from the ISO list or holds an entry that names no single day. Nothing the publisher recorded is dropped.
priorEffectiveDatesRaw.title: Prioreffectivedatesraw

proclamationNumber.description: The proclamation number (`10886` for Proclamation 10886). Set only on proclamations. Memoranda, determinations and notices are not numbered in either series and carry null in both fields, never an invented number. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
proclamationNumber.title: Proclamationnumber

program.description: The benefit or regulatory program a document governs, e.g. Old-Age and Survivors Insurance. 100% populated on Social Security rulings, where it is the primary axis a practitioner filters on. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
program.title: Program

publicLawCites.description:
Structured Statutes at Large citations parsed out of the source credit, populated on ~72% of the US Code. Each entry carries `statVolume`, `statPage`, `type` and a `display` string.

`publicLaws` gives the bare `Pub. L.` list and `sourceCredit` the raw prose; this is the same information already parsed, so a caller can link to the Statutes at Large without re-parsing the credit line. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
publicLawCites.title: Publiclawcites

publicLaws.description: Public Laws referenced by the section, e.g. `['Pub. L. 96-170']`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
publicLaws.title: Publiclaws

publicationDate.description:
The date this document was published by its source. For Federal Register documents this is the FR publication date, the primary citation and sort key, populated on 100% of rules and proposed rules.

Distinct from `effectiveDate` (when it takes legal effect) and from `issueDate` (when the issuing body dated it). A rule is routinely published before it is effective. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
publicationDate.title: Publicationdate

publicationDateRaw.description: The publication date as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `publicationDate`, or null when it is not a date at all.
publicationDateRaw.title: Publicationdateraw

publisherKey.description:
The publisher's own stable identifier for this document, where it issues one. On the US Code this is the OLRC's `usckey` (100% populated), which joins directly to the uscode.house.gov bulk XML; on Colorado regulations it is the state's rule id.

Use it to reconcile our records against the publisher's without matching on citation strings. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
publisherKey.title: Publisherkey

referencedShortTitles.description: Popular names of acts this section REFERENCES, ~10% of the US Code. Distinct from `popularName`, which is the section's own. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
examples: Driftnet Modernization and Bycatch Reduction Act
referencedShortTitles.title: Referencedshorttitles

relatedCitations.description:
Citations OUT of this document that are neither USC nor CFR: the state statutes a regulation implements, the Internal Revenue Code sections a ruling construes, other guidance it points at.

`crossReferencesUsc` and `crossReferencesCfr` are 0% on several of these corpora, so this is the only outbound citation set they have. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
relatedCitations.title: Relatedcitations

relatedDocuments.description: The publisher's own labels for the filings whose text this record carries, in the order the publisher lists them. A CFPB enforcement action is ONE legal event published as two to seventeen PDFs and the unit we serve is the ACTION, not the filing: a consent order and the stipulation consenting to it are one record, because splitting them makes every search return two half-answers. This is what tells you which filings are inside the record you are holding. Only the operative instrument is mirrored under `pdfUrl`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
relatedDocuments.title: Relateddocuments

releaseDate.description: When the document was released publicly, where that differs from when it was issued. NLRB advice memoranda are written years before release; measured, the two dates are never equal. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
releaseDate.title: Releasedate

releaseDateRaw.description: The release date as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `releaseDate`, or null when it is not a date at all.
releaseDateRaw.title: Releasedateraw

relevanceScore.description: Relevance score, normalized to roughly 0-1. Higher means a better match for ranking within one response. It is a relative ranking signal, not a calibrated confidence or probability, so do not compare scores across different queries or treat a fixed value as a quality threshold. Exception: a query that resolves to an exact citation (e.g. '42 U.S.C. § 1983', 'Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5', 'Fed. R. Civ. P. 12') always scores that section 1.0, since it is a certain match rather than a ranked one -- a natural-language or keyword query never returns 1.0 by comparison. null on any endpoint that did not rank: fetching a section by id, a batch fetch, or a section embedded in an intelligence response. When the response carries `rankingDegraded: true`, the relevance model was unavailable and this is a retrieval score on a different, much smaller scale: still a valid ORDER, not a 0-1 relevance.
relevanceScore.title: Relevancescore

renumberedTo.description: Where the publisher says this section went, when `actStatus` is `renumbered`. RAW SOURCE FORM, not an `actId` and not a citation: `self:4651` means section 4651 of this same title, `34:10105` means section 10105 of Title 34. Do not pass it to a section endpoint. Read `renumberedToLabel` instead, or resolve the citation it names through `/us/statutes/resolve`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
renumberedTo.title: Renumberedto

renumberedToLabel.description: `renumberedTo` written out, e.g. `section 10105 of Title 34`. Present whenever `renumberedTo` is. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
renumberedToLabel.title: Renumberedtolabel

requesters.description: Who asked for the determination or relief. On export-control commodity-jurisdiction determinations this is the applicant (100% populated); on no-action letters it determines who may rely on the relief. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
requesters.title: Requesters

rescindedOn.description: The date the document was rescinded or withdrawn, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, when the source states one. See `rescindedOnRaw`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
rescindedOn.title: Rescindedon

rescindedOnRaw.description: The rescission date as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `rescindedOn`.
rescindedOnRaw.title: Rescindedonraw

responseBounds.description: Says whether this response is the whole record. Always present on `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}`; on search, resolve, batch resolve, neighbours and `POST /us/statutes/sections` it appears only on a row that was cut. A heavily amended section (26 U.S.C. 1) carries hundreds of references and a credit line of tens of thousands of characters, so the default response keeps the first 50 items of each long list and the first 4,000 characters of `history`. `truncated` is true when any field was shortened, `fields` lists each with its `total`, what was `returned` and `nextOffset`, and `full=true` on the single-section route returns everything, and the other routes name that call in `note`.

reviewDate.description: The date a rule must be re-adopted or it expires, where the state runs a sunset review. Ohio regulations, ~80% populated. Not an amendment date: it is in the future. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
reviewDate.title: Reviewdate

reviewDateRaw.description: The review date as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `reviewDate`, or null when it is not a date at all.
reviewDateRaw.title: Reviewdateraw

ruleSet.description: For court rules, the rule family this belongs to, e.g. `North Dakota Rules of Civil Procedure`. Rule numbers repeat across families (a Civil Rule 12 and a Criminal Rule 12 both exist), so this is what disambiguates them. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
ruleSet.title: Ruleset

ruleSetCode.description: Stable machine key for the rule family, where `ruleSet` gives only the prose name. 100% populated on the court-rules states that have a rule set. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
ruleSetCode.title: Rulesetcode

sectionNumber.description: Section number (e.g., '1983', '240.10b5-1'). Always present; null when not known.
sectionNumber.title: Sectionnumber

sectionTitle.description: The section's own heading (e.g., 'Rule G. Forfeiture Actions In Rem'). Distinct from `title`, which is the hierarchical display path. Always present; null when not known.
sectionTitle.title: Sectiontitle

settlementAmount.description: The monetary penalty or settlement, as the agency prints it. 95.2% populated on HHS OCR resolution agreements, where it is the single most-asked fact of the corpus. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
settlementAmount.title: Settlementamount

signingDate.description: When a presidential document was signed, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, which is routinely earlier than `publicationDate` and is the legally operative date. See `signingDateRaw`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
signingDate.title: Signingdate

signingDateRaw.description: The signing date as the publisher writes it, present only when it differs from `signingDate`.
signingDateRaw.title: Signingdateraw

source.description:
The named source within `corpusType` this row belongs to, for corpora that fold several bodies of law into one token. Pass it back as the `source` search filter to scope to just this source; the accepted values, with their names, are listed on that filter. Null for corpora with only one source, which includes every state's statutes and regulations.

Not a link, and not where the text came from: it is a filter token. The official link to the publisher's text is `sourceUrl`.
source.title: Source

sourceCharEnd.description: Character offset where this text ends in the source document. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
sourceCharEnd.title: Sourcecharend

sourceCharStart.description: Character offset where this text begins in the source document, for callers reconciling our extraction against the original PDF. Pairs with `sourcePageStart`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
sourceCharStart.title: Sourcecharstart

sourceCredit.description:
The Office of the Law Revision Counsel's credit line for a USC section: the acts that enacted and amended it, in order, e.g. `June 25, 1948, ch. 646, 62 Stat. 869; Pub. L. 85-508, Sec. 12, July 7, 1958, 72 Stat. 348`. Parentheses stripped, whitespace normalized.

USC only, and null on a USC section that prints no credit (a transferred, repealed or reclassified stub). CFR sections carry the same fact as a list in `federalRegisterCitations` instead, which is why the shape differs; no other corpus publishes one. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
sourceCredit.title: Sourcecredit

sourceNote.description: The publisher's source note for the section, verbatim. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
sourceNote.title: Sourcenote

sourcePageEnd.description: Last page in the official PDF; companion to `sourcePageStart`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
sourcePageEnd.title: Sourcepageend

sourcePageStart.description: First page in the official PDF this text was extracted from, for a pinpoint print citation. 100% populated on the Federal Rules. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
sourcePageStart.title: Sourcepagestart

sourceUrl.description:
Where the government published this text: the link to cite and to verify against. The same value `/us/statutes/section/{actId}/body` returns as `sourceUrl`, on every search result, section record and batch item.

It is `externalUrl` when the publisher issued a per-section link, and otherwise falls back to the govinfo.gov page, then the state's own page, then our archived copy of the publisher's page. Null when we hold no publishable link: only official government links are served here.
sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl

sourceUrlNote.description: Says why `sourceUrl` is null. Either we serve no link for this section on purpose and it is cited by `citation` alone, or the publisher issues it only inside a larger file (an archive, spreadsheet or whole volume) that is not a page of the section, or no source link is recorded for it at all. Null when `sourceUrl` is set.
sourceUrlNote.title: Sourceurlnote

state.description: 2-letter lowercase state code (e.g. `ca`, `tx`) when the row belongs to a state corpus. `federal` for federal rows. Always present; null when not known.
state.title: State

stateHtmlUrl.description: HTML rendering of the document. For most state corpora this is the publisher's own page; for corpora we mirror (state agency guidance, regulations, court rules) it is our archived copy of the artifact the publisher served, on statutes-us.vaquill.ai. Use `externalUrl` for the publisher's canonical address. Never a PDF: a mirrored PDF is served as `pdfUrl` instead. Populated for state corpora only. Always present; null when not known.
stateHtmlUrl.title: Statehtmlurl

statutoryAuthority.description: For a CFR/eCFR section: the USC (or other) citations in its 'Authority' note that authorize the rule, e.g. `[{'type': 'usc', 'title': 15, 'section': '78o', 'display': '15 U.S.C. 78o'}]`. Null for non-regulation corpora. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
statutoryAuthority.title: Statutoryauthority

subchapter.description: Subchapter number or identifier. Always present; null when not known.
subchapter.title: Subchapter

subchapterName.description: Subchapter name. Always present; null when not known.
subchapterName.title: Subchaptername

subject.description: The publisher's own subject or document-type label, where it prints one (for example a state insurance bulletin's `RE:` line, or its listing category such as `Rescission`). Omitted from the response when it has no value.
subject.title: Subject

subjectNumber.description: The publisher's numbered subject index entry, the companion to the term in `topics`. 100% populated on Social Security rulings. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
subjectNumber.title: Subjectnumber

subpart.description: Subpart number or identifier (CFR). Always present; null when not known.
subpart.title: Subpart

subpartName.description: Subpart name. Always present; null when not known.
subpartName.title: Subpartname

subtitle.description:
Subtitle, where a jurisdiction puts a level between title and chapter. Maryland's regulations are organised Title > Subtitle > Chapter and are 100% populated; no other served field expressed that level.

Deliberately not the same as `subchapter`, which sits below chapter. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
subtitle.title: Subtitle

subtitleName.description: Subtitle title, the companion to `subtitle`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
subtitleName.title: Subtitlename

supersededBy.description: `actId` of the section that replaced this one. Present on a superseded version so you can fetch the current text in one hop via `GET /statutes/section/{actId}`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
supersededBy.title: Supersededby

supersedes.description: `actId` of the earlier version this section replaced, when known. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
supersedes.title: Supersedes

supersessionActions.description:
What this document does to EARLIER documents, keyed by the issuer's own verb: `modifies`, `obsoletes`, `amplifies`, `clarifies`, `rescinds`, each mapping to the documents affected.

`supersedes` and `supersededBy` cover only the strongest verb. Without these a caller cannot tell a modified revenue procedure from an untouched one, nor see which memorandum rescinded which. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
supersessionActions.title: Supersessionactions

textUrl.description: Plain-text version of the section, from the open-data copy we hold in our own storage. Populated for many state corpora (MS, NJ, NY, NV, etc.) and for United States Code sections. The URL is public by design: the text is open data, so it opens without an API key and carries no credit charge. Null when we hold no plain-text copy. It is never a commercial platform's link.
textUrl.title: Texturl

title.description: Section title. Always present; null when not known.
title.title: Title

titleName.description: Title name (e.g., 'The Public Health and Welfare'). Always present; null when not known.
titleName.title: Titlename

titleNumber.description: USC/CFR/state title number (e.g. '26', '13A'). Always present; null when not known.
titleNumber.title: Titlenumber

topLevelTitle.description:
The outermost division this document sits under, where the corpus has one that `titleNumber`/`chapter`/`part` do not already express. Examples: `Title 9: Criminal` for the DOJ Justice Manual, `Volume 1 - General Policies and Procedures` for the USCIS Policy Manual.

Null for flat corpora, where one document is the whole unit. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
topLevelTitle.title: Topleveltitle

topics.description: The Federal Register's own CFR-index subject terms. Populated on ~71% of rules and ~68% of proposed rules, with one hard boundary: documents published before 2000 carry none, because the Federal Register did not index them this way. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
topics.title: Topics

transferredTo.description: Where the publisher says this section went, when `actStatus` is `transferred`. Same raw source form as `renumberedTo`, and the same warning: it is not an `actId`. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
transferredTo.title: Transferredto

transferredToLabel.description: `transferredTo` written out. Present whenever `transferredTo` is. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
transferredToLabel.title: Transferredtolabel

versionId.description: The publisher's identifier for THIS VERSION of the document, where it versions them separately from the document itself. 100% populated on Colorado regulations, where it is the only version pointer that exists. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
versionId.title: Versionid

volume.description: Volume number for corpora organised in volumes, e.g. the USCIS Policy Manual, whose Volume is the top hierarchy level and had no served representation at all. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
volume.title: Volume

wordCount.description: Words in the full document, so a caller can size a fetch before paying for the body. Omitted from the response when it has no value.
wordCount.title: Wordcount

xmlUrl.description: XML version of the statute section. Always present; null when not known.
xmlUrl.title: Xmlurl

year.description: The year this row was ingested, not the year of the law. Most ingesters stamp the capture year (`time.gmtime().tm_year`) and a few pin a literal, so the bulk of the corpus reads the year it was captured. Do not filter or reason about currency with it. `lastAmendedYear` carries the amendment year, `currentThrough` and `currencyNote` carry the publisher's own currency statement, and `goodLawStatus` carries the status. Always present; null when not known.
year.title: Year

StatuteResult.title: StatuteResult

actStatus.description:
Positively scope to one or more raw publisher statuses, e.g. `"repealed"` to find only dead law, or `["in_force"]` for only sections affirmatively marked current. This is the inverse of `excludeRepealed` and is what you want for a compliance diff that asks what was LOST rather than what remains.

Values are the statuses this API classifies: `abolished`, `deleted`, `expired`, `in_force`, `inactive`, `non_precedential`, `not_funded`, `not_yet_effective`, `omitted`, `proposed`, `recodified`, `recompiled`, `rejected`, `relocated`, `removed`, `renumbered`, `repealed`, `rescinded`, `reserved`, `revoked`, `superseded`, `terminated`, `transferred`, `unconstitutional`, `vacant`, `vacated`, `vetoed`, `withdrawn`. A result's `actStatus` can carry other raw publisher words (`enacted` on session laws, `snapshot`, `pending`); those are not filterable and are rejected with 422, because we cannot say what they mean for whether the law is good. Combining a dead status here with `excludeRepealed: true` contradicts itself and is rejected with 422 rather than silently returning nothing.
actStatus.title: Actstatus

agency.description: Federal Register agency slug, e.g. `environmental-protection-agency`. The agency's full name (`Environmental Protection Agency`) or its Federal Register acronym (`EPA`, `e.p.a.`) resolves to the same slug; an acronym the Federal Register gives to more than one agency (`FS`) or a value naming no agency the corpus holds is a 422, never a charge. Pass a list to match any of several. Applies to `FEDERAL_REGISTER` and `EXECUTIVE_ACTION`; other corpora carry no agency, so combining this with them returns nothing.
agency.title: Agency

article.description:
Scope a search to one or more articles. On `CONSTITUTION` and `STATE_CONSTITUTION` this is the article label as `GET /us/statutes/divisions` lists it (`Amendment XIV`, `Article IV`, `Preamble`). On `STATE` / `REGULATION` it is the article of a code divided by article instead of chapter, such as New York (`2-A` in `ny_jud`). This is the search side of `parent.article`: pass a hit's `parent` straight back to search within its article.

Pass the `identifier` exactly as the listing returned it; a case slip such as `amendment xiv` also matches.
